sentences.zh: ◎忠義下程千里程千里，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: ◎ Loyalty and Righteousness, Lower Section. Cheng Qianli—Cheng Qianli was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Loyalty and Righteousness (continued). Cheng Qianli was a native of Wannian in the Capital district.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，魁岸有力。

translations.literal: He stood seven chi tall, with a towering frame and great strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was seven feet tall, broad-shouldered and powerfully built.

sentences.zh: 應募磧西，累官安西副都護。

translations.literal: He volunteered for service west of the Gobi and rose through successive posts to Vice Protector-General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted in the western frontier armies and eventually became Vice Protector-General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，兼北庭都護、安西北庭節度使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, he additionally held the posts of Protector-General of Beiting and Military Commissioner of Anxi and Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao reign, he also served as Protector-General of Beiting and as military commissioner over Anxi and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 突厥首領阿布思內附，本隸朔方，賜氏李，名獻忠，度屬幽州，素與安祿山有怨，內懼，故叛還磧外，數盜邊。

translations.literal: The Turkic chieftain Abu Si had submitted to the court and originally belonged to Shuofang; he was granted the surname Li and the name Xianzhong, was reassigned to Youzhou jurisdiction, had long harbored resentment against An Lushan, feared him inwardly, and therefore rebelled and returned beyond the desert frontiers, repeatedly raiding the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic leader Abu Si had come over to the Tang and was originally assigned to Shuofang. The court gave him the surname Li and the name Xianzhong and placed him under Youzhou. He had long been at odds with An Lushan and, fearing for his safety, broke away to the outer steppe and repeatedly raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 玄宗患之，詔千里將兵討捕。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was troubled by this and ordered Cheng Qianli to lead troops to pursue and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor, alarmed by these raids, ordered Cheng Qianli to take troops in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 千里諭葛邏祿，陰令掎角。

translations.literal: Cheng Qianli instructed the Geluolu tribe and secretly directed them to attack from a second angle.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qianli persuaded the Geluolu to join the campaign and quietly arranged a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 獻忠果以窮歸葛邏祿，縛之，並妻子帳下數千人送千里所，乃獻俘勤政樓，詔斬以徇。

translations.literal: Xianzhong, driven to extremity, indeed submitted to the Geluolu, who bound him and, together with his wife, children, and several thousand followers in his camp, sent them to Cheng Qianli's headquarters. Thereupon he presented the captive at Qinzheng Tower; an edict ordered him beheaded as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: Hemmed in, Xianzhong fled to the Geluolu, who seized him and, along with his family and several thousand of his followers, delivered the whole party to Cheng Qianli. He then presented the captive at Qinzheng Tower, where an imperial order had him executed as an example.

sentences.zh: 擢千里右金吾衛大將軍，留宿衛。

translations.literal: Cheng Qianli was promoted to Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard and kept on palace night duty.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Qianli was promoted to grand general of the Right Gold Crow Guard and retained at court for palace duty.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，詔募兵河東，即拜節度副使、雲中太守，遷上黨長史。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, an edict called for troops to be raised in Hedong; Cheng Qianli was at once appointed deputy military commissioner and Administrator of Yunzhong, then transferred to be Chief Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, the court ordered troops raised in Hedong. Cheng Qianli was immediately made deputy military commissioner and prefect of Yunzhong, then transferred to chief administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 賊來攻，鏖馘多，累加開府儀同三司、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When the rebels came to attack, he fought fiercely and took many heads; he was repeatedly promoted to Honorary Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Third Rank and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked, he fought hard and killed many of the enemy. He was repeatedly promoted, eventually receiving the honorary title of Splendid Grand Master, Third Rank, and the post of Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，賊將蔡希德圍上黨，輕騎挑戰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, the rebel general Cai Xide besieged Shangdang and sent light cavalry to provoke battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhide reign, the rebel general Cai Xide besieged Shangdang and sent light horsemen to challenge the defenders.

sentences.zh: 千里恃勇開縣門，率百騎欲直禽希德，幾得而救至，乃退。

translations.literal: Relying on his courage, Cheng Qianli opened the county gates, led a hundred horsemen intending to seize Xide directly, and had almost succeeded when rescuers arrived, whereupon he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in his own valor, Cheng Qianli opened the county gates and led a hundred horsemen in a dash to capture Cai Xide. He nearly succeeded, but enemy reinforcements arrived and he was forced to pull back.

sentences.zh: 會橋壞，馬顛，為賊執，仰首敕諸騎使還，曰：「為我報諸將，可失帥，不可失城。」

translations.literal: It happened that a bridge collapsed; his horse stumbled, and he was seized by the rebels. Lifting his head, he ordered the horsemen to return, saying: "Report to the generals for me: one may lose a commander, but one must not lose the city."
translations.idiomatic: Just then a bridge gave way; his horse stumbled and he was taken by the rebels. He raised his head and ordered his men to ride back, saying, "Tell the generals for me: you may lose your commander, but you must not lose the city."

sentences.zh: 軍中皆為泣下，增備固守。

translations.literal: The whole army wept; they strengthened their defenses and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army wept. The garrison redoubled its defenses and held the city.

sentences.zh: 賊不能下，乃還。

translations.literal: The rebels could not take the city and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to capture the city, the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 囚千里至東都，安慶緒偽署特進，囚客省。

translations.literal: They imprisoned Cheng Qianli and brought him to the Eastern Capital; An Qingxu falsely appointed him Special Grand Master and confined him in the Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Cheng Qianli to the Eastern Capital. An Qingxu gave him the empty title of Special Grand Master and kept him imprisoned in the Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 慶緒敗，為嚴莊所害。

translations.literal: When Qingxu was defeated, Cheng Qianli was killed by Yan Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu fell, Yan Zhuang had him killed.

sentences.zh: 後赦令數下，追褒死難者，惟千里生見執，不及云。

translations.literal: Later, amnesty edicts were repeatedly issued to posthumously honor those who died in the calamity, but Cheng Qianli alone, having been captured alive, was not included.
translations.idiomatic: Later, repeated amnesties posthumously honored those who had died in the rebellion, but Cheng Qianli alone—because he had been taken alive—was not mentioned.

sentences.zh: 附 袁光廷初，祿山構難，西北戍兵悉入援，故河、隴郡縣皆陷吐蕃，惟河西戍將袁光廷為伊州刺史，固守歷年，雖遊說百緒，終不降，諸下同心無攜畔者。

translations.literal: Appended: Yuan Guangting. At the beginning, when Lushan stirred up trouble, the northwestern garrison troops all marched east to reinforce the capital, so the commanderies and counties of He and Long all fell to the Tibetans. Only the Hexi garrison commander Yuan Guangting, as Administrator of Yizhou, held firm for years; though enticed by every sort of persuasion, he never submitted, and all his subordinates were of one mind without defection.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Yuan Guangting. When An Lushan first raised the rebellion, the northwestern frontier garrisons were all drawn east to reinforce the capital, and the prefectures of He and Long fell to Tibet. Only Yuan Guangting, a Hexi garrison officer serving as prefect of Yizhou, held out year after year. Every kind of persuasion was tried, yet he would not surrender, and his officers and men stood together without a single defection.

sentences.zh: 及糧竭，手殺妻子，自焚死。

translations.literal: When provisions were exhausted, he personally killed his wife and children and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran out, he killed his wife and children with his own hand and then burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 建中初，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 龐堅龐堅，京兆涇陽人。

translations.literal: Pang Jian—Pang Jian was a native of Jingyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jian was a native of Jingyang in the Capital district.

sentences.zh: 四世祖玉，事隋為監門直閣。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Yu served the Sui as a Direct Attendant of the Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Yu had served the Sui as a direct attendant in the Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 李密據洛口，玉以關中銳兵屬王世充擊之，百戰不衄。

translations.literal: When Li Mi held Luokou, Yu led the elite troops of Guanzhong under Wang Shichong to attack him and fought a hundred battles without defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi held Luokou, Yu led Guanzhong's best troops under Wang Shichong to attack him and fought a hundred engagements without a setback.

sentences.zh: 世充歸東都，秦王東徇洛，玉率萬騎降，高祖以隋舊臣，禮之。

translations.literal: When Shichong returned to the Eastern Capital, the Prince of Qin marched east against Luoyang; Yu led ten thousand horsemen to surrender, and Gaozu, treating him as a former Sui minister, honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong withdrew to the Eastern Capital and the Prince of Qin marched east against Luoyang, Yu surrendered with ten thousand horsemen. Gaozu received him with full honors befitting a former Sui official.

sentences.zh: 玉魁梧有力，明軍法，久宿衛，習知朝廷制度。

translations.literal: Yu was tall and powerful, versed in military law, long stationed in palace guard duty, and thoroughly familiar with court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was tall and strong, skilled in military regulations, and had long served in the palace guards, so he knew court protocol inside out.

sentences.zh: 帝顧諸將多不閑儀檢，故授玉領軍、武衛二大將軍，使眾觀以為模矱，出為梁州總管。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw that many generals were unskilled in ceremony and decorum, so he appointed Yu Grand General of the Central Army and of the Martial Guard, that the multitude might observe him as a model, then sent him out as Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that many of his generals were careless about ceremony and decorum, the Emperor made Yu grand general of both the Central Army and the Martial Guard so that others might take him as a model, then sent him out as commander-in-chief of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 巴山獠叛，玉梟其首，餘黨四奔，屬縣獠與反者州裏親戚為賊遊說，言不可窮躡。

translations.literal: The Liao of Bashan rebelled; Yu beheaded their leader, and the rest scattered in flight. Liao in subordinate counties who were kin by neighborhood to the rebels went among the bandits to plead, saying they must not be pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao of Bashan rebelled, Yu cut off the head of their leader and the rest fled in all directions. Liao in neighboring counties who were related to the rebels went among the bandits to plead that pursuit must not be pressed to the bitter end.

sentences.zh: 玉不聽，下令軍中曰：「谷熟，吾盡收以饋軍。

translations.literal: Yu would not listen and issued an order in the army, saying: "When the grain ripens, I shall gather it all to feed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yu refused to listen and issued an order throughout the army: "When the grain ripens, I shall take it all to feed my soldiers.

sentences.zh: 非盡賊，吾不反。」

translations.literal: Unless the bandits are utterly destroyed, I shall not return."
translations.idiomatic: Unless every last bandit is destroyed, I will not turn back."

sentences.zh: 聞者懼，相謂曰：「軍不止，吾谷盡，且餓死。」

translations.literal: Those who heard were afraid and said to one another: "If the army does not stop, our grain will all be gone and we shall starve."
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were terrified and said to one another, "If the army does not stop, our grain will be gone and we shall starve."

sentences.zh: 乃共入賊營，與所親相結，斬渠長以降，眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Thereupon they all entered the rebel camp together, joined with their kin inside, beheaded the chieftain and submitted; the multitude then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: They then entered the rebel camp together, joined forces with their relatives inside, killed the chieftain, and surrendered. The whole force broke apart.

sentences.zh: 徙越州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Regional Commander of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 召為監門大將軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as Grand General of the Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as grand general of the Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 太宗以耆厚，令主東宮兵。

translations.literal: Taizong, considering him aged and steady, put him in charge of the Eastern Palace troops.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, trusting his age and steadiness, put him in charge of the crown prince's guard.

sentences.zh: 雖老不怠，小大之務無不親。

translations.literal: Though old, he did not slacken; he personally attended to affairs great and small.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, he never slackened and personally oversaw every matter, large or small.

sentences.zh: 卒，帝為廢朝，贈幽州都督、工部尚書。

translations.literal: When he died, the Emperor suspended court for a day and posthumously made him Regional Commander of Youzhou and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the Emperor suspended court for a day and posthumously appointed him regional commander of Youzhou and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 堅歷潁川太守。

translations.literal: Jian had served as Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Jian had previously served as prefect of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，南陽節度使魯炅表堅為長史兼防禦副使，以薛願為潁川太守，共守潁川。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Lu Kui, Military Commissioner of Nanyang, memorialized to appoint Jian Chief Administrator and Deputy Commissioner for Defense, with Xue Yuan as Administrator of Yingchuan, to defend Yingchuan together.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Lu Kui, military commissioner of Nanyang, recommended Pang Jian as chief administrator and deputy commissioner for defense, with Xue Yuan as prefect of Yingchuan, and the two jointly defended the city.

sentences.zh: 時陳留、滎陽已陷賊，南陽被圍，而潁川當往來劇。

translations.literal: At that time Chenliu and Xingyang had already fallen to the rebels, Nanyang was besieged, and Yingchuan lay on the busiest route of traffic.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu and Xingyang had already fallen, Nanyang was under siege, and Yingchuan lay on the busiest corridor of rebel movement.

sentences.zh: 賊將阿史那承慶悉銳攻之，傅城百里，樹木皆刊。

translations.literal: The rebel general Ashina Chengqing attacked with all his elite forces, encamping for a hundred li around the city; every tree was cut down.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Ashina Chengqing attacked with his best troops, encamping for a hundred li around the city and felling every tree in sight.

sentences.zh: 城中士單寡，糧少，而願、堅晝夜戰，諸郡兵無援者，自正月盡十一月。

translations.literal: The defenders in the city were few and provisions scant, yet Yuan and Jian fought day and night; no troops from other commanderies came to their aid, from the first month through the eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison was thin and food was short, yet Yuan and Jian fought day and night. No relief came from neighboring commanderies, from the first month through the eleventh.

sentences.zh: 賊設木鵝、沖車、飛梯薄城，矢如雨，士皆雷噪，夜半逾城入，二人不肯降。

translations.literal: The rebels deployed wooden geese, battering rams, and flying ladders against the walls; arrows fell like rain; the soldiers all roared like thunder. At midnight they scaled the walls and entered, but the two men would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels brought up wooden geese, battering rams, and flying ladders. Arrows fell like rain; the defenders roared like thunder. At midnight the enemy scaled the walls and broke in, but the two commanders still refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 賊縛致東京，將礫解之，有說祿山曰：「義士也，彼為其主，殺之不詳。」

translations.literal: The rebels bound them and sent them to the Eastern Capital, intending to dismember them alive. Someone said to Lushan: "They are righteous men; they acted for their lord. To kill them would be inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bound them and sent them to the Eastern Capital, intending to dismember them alive. Someone told An Lushan, "These are men of loyalty who died for their lord. To kill them would bring ill fortune."

sentences.zh: 乃縛於樹。

translations.literal: They were therefore bound to trees instead.
translations.idiomatic: They were bound to trees instead.

sentences.zh: 比且死，見者哭之。

translations.literal: As they were about to die, all who saw them wept.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached, all who saw them wept.

sentences.zh: 附 薛願願，汾陰人。

translations.literal: Appended: Xue Yuan—Yuan was a native of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Xue Yuan was a native of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 父縚，太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Tao was Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao had been Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 兄崇一，娶惠宣太子女，其女弟為太子瑛妃。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chongyi married a daughter of the Huixuan Princess; his younger sister became consort to the Crown Prince Ying.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chongyi married a daughter of Princess Huixuan, and his younger sister became a consort of Crown Prince Ying.

sentences.zh: 瑛廢，貶願嶺外，久乃得還。

translations.literal: When Ying was deposed, Yuan was banished beyond the Ling ranges and only after a long time was he able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ying was deposed, Yuan was exiled beyond the Ling ranges and was not able to return until many years later.

sentences.zh: 張興張興者，束鹿人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xing—Zhang Xing was a native of Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing was a native of Shulu.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，一飯至斗米，肉十斤。

translations.literal: He stood seven chi tall; in a single meal he could consume a dou of rice and ten jin of meat.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet tall and could eat a dou of rice and ten jin of meat in a single meal.

sentences.zh: 悍趫而辯，為饒陽裨將。

translations.literal: Fierce, swift, and eloquent, he served as a deputy general of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, quick, and eloquent, he served as a deputy general at Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，攻饒陽。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he attacked Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he attacked Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 興開張禍福，譬曉敵人，而嬰城彌年，眾心遂固。

translations.literal: Xing set forth fortune and misfortune at length and lectured the enemy with analogies; the city was held fast for a full year, and the people's resolve thereby grew firm.
translations.idiomatic: Xing harangued the enemy at length on the consequences of their rebellion, and the city held out for a full year until the people's resolve was unshakable.

sentences.zh: 滄、趙已隱，史思明引眾傅城，興擐甲持陌刀重十五斤乘城。

translations.literal: Cang and Zhao had already fallen; Shi Siming led his forces to encamp against the walls. Xing donned armor, took up a mo-blade weighing fifteen jin, and mounted the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou and Zhao had already fallen. Shi Siming brought his army to the walls. Xing put on armor, took up a fifteen-jin mo-blade, and climbed to the battlements.

sentences.zh: 賊將入，興一舉刀，輒數人死，賊皆氣懾。

translations.literal: As the rebels were about to enter, with one sweep of his blade Xing killed several men at a stroke; the rebels were all cowed in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels pressed in, a single stroke of his blade killed several men at once, and the enemy's spirit broke.

sentences.zh: 城破，思明縛之馬前，好謂曰：「將軍壯士，能屈節，當受高爵。」

translations.literal: When the city fell, Siming bound him before his horse and spoke kindly, saying: "General, you are a stalwart man. If you can bend your will, you shall receive a lofty rank."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Siming bound him before his horse and spoke kindly: "General, you are a brave man. Bend your will and you shall receive a high rank."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔嚴顏一巴郡將，猶不降張飛。

translations.literal: He replied: "In former times Yan Yan was only a commandery general of Ba, yet he still would not submit to Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Long ago Yan Yan was only a commandery general in Ba, yet he still refused to bow to Zhang Fei.

sentences.zh: 我大郡將，安能委身逆虜？

translations.literal: I am a grand commandery general—how could I yield myself to a rebel barbarian?
translations.idiomatic: I am a grand commandery general. How could I submit to a rebel?

sentences.zh: 今日幸得死，然願以一言為誡。」

translations.literal: Today I am fortunate enough to die, yet I wish to leave one word as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Today I am fortunate enough to die, but I would leave you one word of warning."

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「云何？」

translations.literal: Siming said: "What is it?"
translations.idiomatic: Siming asked, "What is it?"

sentences.zh: 興曰：「天子遇祿山如父子，今乃反。

translations.literal: Xing said: "The Son of Heaven treated Lushan like father and son, yet now he has rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "The Son of Heaven treated An Lushan as a father treats a son, yet now he has rebelled.

sentences.zh: 大丈夫不能為國掃除，反為其下，何哉？」

translations.literal: A great man who cannot purge the realm for his country but instead serves beneath him—what sort of thing is that?"
translations.idiomatic: A true man who cannot clear the realm for his country but instead serves beneath such a man—what sort of man is that?"

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「將軍不觀天道邪？

translations.literal: Siming said: "General, do you not observe the mandate of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Siming said, "General, have you not seen Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 吾上起兵二十萬，直趣洛陽，天下大定。

translations.literal: Our lord raised an army of two hundred thousand and marched straight on Luoyang; the realm was largely settled.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord raised two hundred thousand men and marched straight on Luoyang. The realm was nearly settled.

sentences.zh: 以偏師叩函谷，守將面縛，唐亡固矣。」

translations.literal: With a detached column he struck at Hangu Pass; the defending general bound himself and came forward—the Tang's fall was already assured."
translations.idiomatic: A detached force struck Hangu Pass and the defenders came out with hands bound. The Tang's fall was already certain."

sentences.zh: 興曰：「桀、紂、秦、隋窮人力，舉四海與為怨，故商、周、漢、唐因得代之而有神器。

translations.literal: Xing said: "Jie, Zhou, the Qin, and the Sui exhausted human strength and made the four seas their enemies; therefore Shang, Zhou, Han, and Tang were able to replace them and receive the sacred regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, "Jie, Zhou, the Qin, and the Sui exhausted the people's strength and turned the whole realm against them. That is how Shang, Zhou, Han, and Tang were able to replace them and take the throne.

sentences.zh: 皇帝無違德，祿山非數帝賢，是茍延歲月，終即禽耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor has no transgression in virtue; Lushan is no sage among successive emperors—he merely prolongs his days, and in the end he will be captured."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor has done no wrong, and An Lushan is no sage among emperors. He merely drags out his days; in the end he will be taken."

sentences.zh: 思明怒，鋸解之。

translations.literal: Siming was enraged and had him sawn apart.
translations.idiomatic: Siming flew into a rage and had him sawn apart.

sentences.zh: 且死，罵曰：「吾能裒強死兵敗賊眾！」

translations.literal: As he was about to die, he cursed, saying: "I could gather the strong and die fighting to defeat the rebel host!"
translations.idiomatic: As he was dying he cursed, "I could rally the strong, die fighting, and break the rebel host!"

sentences.zh: 軍中凜然為改容。

translations.literal: The whole army was awestruck and their faces changed.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army was struck with awe.

sentences.zh: 蔡廷玉蔡廷玉，幽州昌平人。

translations.literal: Cai Tingyu—Cai Tingyu was a native of Changping in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Tingyu was a native of Changping in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 事安祿山，未有聞。

translations.literal: He had served An Lushan, but nothing noteworthy is recorded of him.
translations.idiomatic: He had served An Lushan, but nothing noteworthy is recorded of him before this.

sentences.zh: 與朱泚同里闬，少相狎近，泚為幽州節度使，秦署幕府。

translations.literal: He was from the same neighborhood as Zhu Ci; in youth they were intimate. When Ci became Military Commissioner of Youzhou, he appointed Tingyu to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: He came from the same neighborhood as Zhu Ci and had been close to him since youth. When Zhu Ci became military commissioner of Youzhou, he took Tingyu onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 廷玉有沈略，善與人交，內外愛附。

translations.literal: Tingyu was deep in counsel and skilled at making friends; within and without, all were fond of him and attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu was shrewd and skilled at winning people over; everyone inside and outside Zhu Ci's circle liked and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 泚多所叩咨，數遣至京師。

translations.literal: Ci often sought his advice and repeatedly sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci often sought his counsel and repeatedly sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 當是時，幽州兵最強，財雄，士驕悍，日思吞並，不知有上下禮法。

translations.literal: At that time the Youzhou troops were the strongest, their wealth abundant; the soldiers were proud and fierce, daily scheming to swallow up others, and ignorant of the rites and laws between superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Youzhou army was the strongest force in the realm and flush with wealth. Its soldiers were proud and fierce, constantly scheming to swallow up neighboring territories, and cared nothing for the rites between sovereign and subject.

sentences.zh: 廷玉間語泚曰：「古未有不臣而能推福及子孫者。

translations.literal: Tingyu occasionally said to Ci: "Since antiquity there has never been one who, while unsubmissive, could extend blessings to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time Tingyu told Zhu Ci, "Since antiquity no one who refused to serve his sovereign has ever secured blessings for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 公南聯趙、魏，北奚虜，兵我地險，然非永安計，一日趙、魏反噬，公乃沸鼎魚耳。

translations.literal: Your Grace links Zhao and Wei to the south and the Xi barbarians to the north; our troops are strong and our terrain perilous—yet this is no plan for lasting peace. One day Zhao and Wei will turn and bite back, and Your Grace will be a fish in a boiling cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: You are allied with Zhao and Wei to the south and the Xi to the north. Your troops are strong and your terrain defensible, yet this is no plan for lasting security. One day Zhao and Wei will turn on you, and you will be a fish in a boiling pot.

sentences.zh: 不如奉天子，多難，可勒勛鼎彜，若何？」

translations.literal: Better to serve the Son of Heaven; amid many troubles, you could inscribe your merit on the bronze tripod—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: Better to serve the Son of Heaven. In these troubled times you could win merit recorded on the royal tripods. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 泚善之。

translations.literal: Ci approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 廷玉陰欲耗其力，則諷泚出金幣禮士，又勸歸貢賦助天子經費，獻牛馬系道，儲廥為單。

translations.literal: Tingyu secretly wished to drain Ci's strength, so he urged Ci to spend gold and coin honoring scholars, and also advised returning tribute and taxes to aid the Son of Heaven's expenses. Oxen and horses lined the roads in tribute; the granaries stood nearly empty.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly wishing to drain Zhu Ci's strength, Tingyu urged him to spend gold honoring scholars and to return tribute and taxes to support the court. Oxen and horses lined the roads as tribute, and the granaries were nearly emptied.

sentences.zh: 因勸泚入朝，泚將聽，諸校怒，縛廷玉辱之，廷玉無橈辭，泚不忍殺，囚歲餘出之，謂曰：「而亦悔乎？」

translations.literal: He then urged Ci to go to court. Ci was about to comply when the officers were enraged, bound Tingyu, and humiliated him. Tingyu would not bend in speech. Ci could not bear to kill him and imprisoned him for more than a year before releasing him, saying: "Do you also regret it now?"
translations.idiomatic: He then urged Zhu Ci to go to court. Zhu Ci was about to agree when his officers grew furious, bound Tingyu, and humiliated him. Tingyu would not yield a word. Zhu Ci could not bring himself to kill him and kept him imprisoned for more than a year before releasing him and asking, "Do you regret it now?"

sentences.zh: 廷玉曰：「導公為逆即悔，勉公以義何悔為？」

translations.literal: Tingyu said: "If I had led Your Grace into rebellion, I would regret it; but in urging Your Grace toward righteousness, what is there to regret?"
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu said, "I would regret it if I had led you into rebellion. But in urging you toward righteousness, what is there to regret?"

sentences.zh: 復縶滿歲，問曰：「能省過否？

translations.literal: He was bound again for a full year. Ci asked: "Can you reflect on your faults?
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned again for a full year. Zhu Ci asked, "Can you admit your fault?

sentences.zh: 不爾，且死。」

translations.literal: If not, you shall soon die."
translations.idiomatic: If not, you will die."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不殺我，公得名。

translations.literal: He replied: "If you do not kill me, Your Grace will gain a name.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If you do not kill me, you will gain a reputation.

sentences.zh: 殺我，吾得名。」

translations.literal: If you kill me, I shall gain a name."
translations.idiomatic: If you kill me, I shall gain a reputation."

sentences.zh: 泚不能屈，待如初。

translations.literal: Ci could not break him and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci could not break him and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 又有朱體微者，亦泚腹心。

translations.literal: There was also Zhu Tiwei, likewise a trusted confidant of Ci.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhu Tiwei, another of Zhu Ci's trusted confidants.

sentences.zh: 廷玉有建白，體微輒左右之，故泚愈信，桀傲稍革。

translations.literal: Whenever Tingyu made a proposal, Tiwei would support it on either side; therefore Ci trusted him all the more, and his arrogance was gradually reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tingyu made a proposal, Tiwei would second it, so Zhu Ci trusted them all the more and his arrogance was gradually curbed.

sentences.zh: 廷玉遂蕆朝事。

translations.literal: Tingyu thereupon oversaw court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu thus came to oversee affairs at court.

sentences.zh: 泚乃奏涿州為永泰軍，薊州靜塞軍，瀛州清夷軍，莫州唐興軍，置團練使，以支郡隸屬，盧龍軍稍削。

translations.literal: Ci then memorialized to make Zhuozhou the Yongtai Army, Jizhou the Jingsai Army, Yingzhou the Qingyi Army, and Mozhou the Tangxing Army, appointing training commissioners so that subordinate commanderies were placed under their jurisdiction; the Lulong Army was thereby gradually reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci then memorialized to establish Zhuozhou as the Yongtai Army, Jizhou as the Jingsai Army, Yingzhou as the Qingyi Army, and Mozhou as the Tangxing Army, each with a training commissioner so that neighboring commanderies were placed under their jurisdiction. The Lulong Army was thus gradually weakened.

sentences.zh: 而泚內畏弟滔逼己，滔亦勸泚入朝，乃以軍屬滔。

translations.literal: Yet Ci inwardly feared his younger brother Tao pressing upon him; Tao also urged Ci to go to court, and Ci therefore entrusted the army to Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhu Ci inwardly feared his younger brother Zhu Tao, who also urged him to go to court, and Zhu Ci therefore entrusted the army to him.

sentences.zh: 廷玉、體微共白泚：「公入朝為功臣首，後務至重，須誠信者乃可付。

translations.literal: Tingyu and Tiwei jointly told Ci: "When Your Grace goes to court as foremost among the meritorious, affairs afterward will be weighty indeed; only a man of sincerity and trust may be entrusted with them.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu and Tiwei jointly told Zhu Ci, "When you go to court as the foremost of the meritorious, the affairs you leave behind will be weighty indeed. Only a man of sincerity and trust can be entrusted with them.

sentences.zh: 滔雖大弟，多變不情，如假以兵，是嫁之禍也。」

translations.literal: Though Tao is the elder brother, he is changeable and without feeling; if you lend him troops, it is handing him the means of disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Though Tao is your elder brother, he is fickle and ruthless. If you give him the army, you are handing him the means of your own ruin."

sentences.zh: 泚不聽。

translations.literal: Ci would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci would not listen.

sentences.zh: 二人隨泚到朝，德宗為太子時，知廷玉名，及見，禮眷殊渥。

translations.literal: The two men followed Ci to court. When Dezong was still crown prince, he had known Tingyu's name; when they met, the favor and regard shown him were exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: The two men accompanied Zhu Ci to court. Dezong had known Tingyu's name since his days as crown prince, and when they met he treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 泚統幽州行營為涇原鳳翔節度使，詔廷玉以大理少卿為司馬，體微為要籍。

translations.literal: Ci took command of the Youzhou field army as Military Commissioner of Jingyuan and Fengxiang; an edict appointed Tingyu Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review as army deputy, and Tiwei as chief registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci took command of the Youzhou field army as military commissioner of Jingyuan and Fengxiang. Tingyu was appointed army deputy with the rank of vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and Tiwei was made chief registrar.

sentences.zh: 滔有請於泚，或不順，廷玉必折之，俾循故法。

translations.literal: When Tao made requests of Ci that were sometimes not in accord, Tingyu would always refute them and make him follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhu Tao made requests of Zhu Ci that went against established practice, Tingyu would overrule them and make him follow the old rules.

sentences.zh: 滔已破田悅，浸傲肆自用。

translations.literal: Tao had already defeated Tian Yue and gradually grew arrogant, willful, and self-willed.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Tian Yue, Zhu Tao grew increasingly arrogant and willful.

sentences.zh: 左右有惡廷玉者，妄云：「素毀滔，欲四分燕，廷玉倡之，體微和之。」

translations.literal: Those around him who bore ill will toward Tingyu falsely said: "He has long slandered Tao and wishes to divide Yan into four parts; Tingyu initiated this and Tiwei seconded it."
translations.idiomatic: Those around Zhu Tao who hated Tingyu spread a false report: "He has long slandered Tao and wants to divide Yan into four parts. Tingyu started it and Tiwei backed him."

sentences.zh: 滔表言二人離間骨肉，請殺於有司。

translations.literal: Tao memorialized that the two men had estranged flesh and blood and requested that they be executed by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao memorialized that the two men had driven a wedge between brothers and asked that they be put to death by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 亦遺泚書云云。

translations.literal: He also sent Ci a letter to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Zhu Ci a letter to the same effect.

sentences.zh: 泚恚滔奪其軍，不從。

translations.literal: Ci resented Tao for seizing his army and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci resented Zhu Tao for taking his army and refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 會滔以幽州叛，帝示滔表，而泚亦白髮其書，乃歸罪於二人，貶廷玉柳州司戶參軍、體微南浦尉以慰滔。

translations.literal: It happened that Tao rebelled with Youzhou. The Emperor showed Tao's memorial, and Ci also reported the letter he had sent; blame was then placed on the two men. Tingyu was demoted to Revenue Assistant of Liuzhou and Tiwei to Captain of Nanpu to appease Tao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao rebelled with Youzhou, the Emperor showed his memorial and Zhu Ci also reported the letter he had sent. Blame was placed on the two men. Tingyu was demoted to revenue assistant of Liuzhou and Tiwei to captain of Nanpu to appease Zhu Tao.

sentences.zh: 滔使諜伺諸朝，曰：「上若不殺廷玉，當謫去，得東出洛，我且縛致麾下支解之。」

translations.literal: Tao sent spies to watch affairs at court, saying: "If the sovereign does not kill Tingyu, he will surely be banished. If he gets out east of Luoyang, I shall bind him and bring him under my command to dismember him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao sent spies to watch the court, saying, "If the Emperor does not kill Tingyu, he will be banished. If he gets east of Luoyang, I shall seize him and dismember him before my troops."

sentences.zh: 將行，帝勞廷玉曰：「爾姑行，為國受屈，歲中當還。」

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the Emperor comforted Tingyu, saying: "Go for now; you are suffering disgrace for the state. Within the year you shall return."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, the Emperor comforted him: "Go for now. You are suffering disgrace for the state. You shall return within the year."

sentences.zh: 遷玉至藍田驛，人白左巡使鄭詹：「商於道險，不可往。」

translations.literal: As Tingyu was being transferred to Lantian Post Station, someone informed the Left Patrol Commissioner Zheng Zhan: "The Shangyu road is perilous; he must not go that way."
translations.idiomatic: At Lantian Post Station someone informed the Left Patrol Commissioner Zheng Zhan, "The Shangyu road is dangerous. He must not be sent that way."

sentences.zh: 詹追使趨潼關。

translations.literal: Zhan sent pursuers to hurry the escort toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan sent pursuers to hurry the escort toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 廷玉告子少誠、少良曰：「我為天子不血刃下幽十一城，欲裂其壤，使不得桀，而敗於將成，天助逆邪？

translations.literal: Tingyu told his sons Shaocheng and Shaoliang: "I brought eleven cities of You down for the Son of Heaven without drawing a blade, intending to split their territory so they could not grow arrogant, yet failed on the verge of success—is Heaven aiding the rebels?
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu told his sons Shaocheng and Shaoliang, "I brought eleven cities of You under the Son of Heaven without drawing a blade, intending to split their territory so they could not grow arrogant, yet failed on the verge of success. Is Heaven aiding the rebels?

sentences.zh: 今吏使我出東都，此殆滔計，吾不可以辱國。」

translations.literal: Now the officials are sending me out toward the Eastern Capital—this is likely Tao's scheme. I cannot bring disgrace upon the state."
translations.idiomatic: Now the officials are sending me out toward the Eastern Capital. This is likely Zhu Tao's scheme. I cannot bring disgrace upon the state."

sentences.zh: 比至靈寶，自投於河。

translations.literal: When he reached Lingbao, he threw himself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Lingbao, he threw himself into the river.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧杞方疾御史大夫嚴郢，欲逐之，得廷玉死狀，即抵詹死，而斥出郢。

translations.literal: The chief minister Lu Qi was at that time hostile toward the Censor-in-Chief Yan Ying and wished to drive him out. Learning of Tingyu's death, he immediately charged Zhan with capital guilt and expelled Yan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Lu Qi was at odds with Censor-in-Chief Yan Ying and wished to drive him out. Learning of Tingyu's death, he immediately had Zhan charged with capital guilt and expelled Yan Ying.

sentences.zh: 帝閔廷玉忠，歸其柩，厚賻之。

translations.literal: The Emperor pitied Tingyu's loyalty, had his coffin returned, and gave a generous funeral grant.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pitied Tingyu's loyalty, had his coffin returned, and gave a generous funeral grant.

sentences.zh: 李晟平朱泚，少誠等適終喪，晟表丐追贈廷玉。

translations.literal: When Li Sheng pacified Zhu Ci, Shaocheng and the others had just completed mourning; Sheng memorialized requesting posthumous honors for Tingyu.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sheng pacified Zhu Ci, Shaocheng and his brothers had just completed mourning. Sheng memorialized requesting posthumous honors for Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 並官二子。

translations.literal: Both sons were given official posts.
translations.idiomatic: Both sons were given official posts.

sentences.zh: 而帝方招來滔，寢其奏，遂已。

translations.literal: But the Emperor was then seeking to win Tao back and shelved the memorial; the matter ended there.
translations.idiomatic: But the Emperor was then seeking to win Zhu Tao back and shelved the memorial. The matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 符令奇符令奇，沂州臨沂人。

translations.literal: Fu Lingqi—Fu Lingqi was a native of Linyi in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lingqi was a native of Linyi in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初為盧龍軍裨將。

translations.literal: He first served as a deputy general of the Lulong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a deputy general in the Lulong Army.

sentences.zh: 會幽州亂，挈子璘奔昭義，節度使薛嵩署為軍副。

translations.literal: When Youzhou fell into turmoil, he took his son Lin and fled to Zhaoyi; the Military Commissioner Xue Song appointed him army deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou fell into turmoil, he took his son Lin and fled to Zhaoyi, where Military Commissioner Xue Song appointed him army deputy.

sentences.zh: 嵩卒，田承嗣盜其地，引令奇為右職。

translations.literal: When Song died, Tian Chengsi seized his territory and brought Lingqi into a senior post.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Song died, Tian Chengsi seized his territory and brought Lingqi into a senior post.

sentences.zh: 田悅拒命，馬燧敗之洹水。

translations.literal: Tian Yue defied orders; Ma Sui defeated him at the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue defied the court's orders, and Ma Sui defeated him at the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 令奇密語璘曰：「吾閱世事多矣。

translations.literal: Lingqi spoke secretly to Lin, saying: "I have seen much of the affairs of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqi spoke secretly to Lin: "I have seen much of the world in my time.

sentences.zh: 自安、史幹紀，無噍類。

translations.literal: Since An and Shi stirred up their age, none have been left alive.
translations.idiomatic: Since An Lushan and Shi Siming stirred up their age, none of their followers have been left alive.

sentences.zh: 吾觀田氏覆亡無時，安用茍旦夕，系縲京師，宗族屠地？

translations.literal: I see the Tian clan's destruction as imminent—why cling to a few more days and nights, end up bound in the capital, and have your clan's lands put to the sword?
translations.idiomatic: I see the Tian clan's destruction as imminent. Why cling to a few more days only to end up bound in the capital with your whole clan put to the sword?

sentences.zh: 汝能委質朝廷，為唐忠臣，吾亦名揚後世矣。」

translations.literal: If you can submit your allegiance to the court and become a loyal minister of Tang, my name too will shine in later ages."
translations.idiomatic: If you can submit to the court and become a loyal minister of Tang, my name too will shine in later ages."

sentences.zh: 璘泣曰：「悅，忍人也，近禍可畏。」

translations.literal: Lin wept and said: "Yue is a ruthless man; imminent disaster is to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: Lin wept and said, "Yue is a ruthless man. Imminent disaster is to be feared."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「今王師四合，吾屬俎中醢。

translations.literal: He replied: "Now the imperial armies close in from all four sides; we are meat on the chopping block.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The imperial armies close in from all four sides. We are meat on the chopping block.

sentences.zh: 兒今行，吾死不朽；

translations.literal: If you go now, my death will not be in vain;
translations.idiomatic: If you go now, my death will not be in vain.

sentences.zh: 不行，吾亦死。

translations.literal: if you do not go, I shall die all the same.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not go, I shall die all the same.

sentences.zh: 屍疊逆地云何？」

translations.literal: What good is it to pile corpses upon rebel ground?"
translations.idiomatic: What good is it to pile corpses upon rebel ground?"

sentences.zh: 璘俯泣不能對。

translations.literal: Lin bowed his head and wept, unable to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Lin bowed his head and wept, unable to reply.

sentences.zh: 初，悅與李納會濮陽，因乞師，納分麾下隨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yue had met Li Na at Puyang and requested troops; Na detached men from his command to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tian Yue had met Li Na at Puyang and requested troops. Na detached men from his command to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 至是，納兵歸齊，使璘以三百騎護送。

translations.literal: At this time Na's troops were returning to Qi, and he had Lin escort them with three hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Na's troops were returning to Qi, and he had Lin escort them with three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 璘與父嚙臂別，乃以眾降燧。

translations.literal: Lin and his father bit their arms in parting; then he led his force to surrender to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and his father bit their arms in farewell, then he led his force to surrender to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 璘之出，與三子同降。

translations.literal: When Lin went out, his three sons surrendered with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin went out, his three sons surrendered with him.

sentences.zh: 悅怒，引令奇切讓。

translations.literal: Yue was enraged and summoned Lingqi to rebuke him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was enraged and summoned Lingqi to rebuke him sharply.

sentences.zh: 令奇罵曰：「爾忘義背主，旦夕死。

translations.literal: Lingqi cursed him, saying: "You have forgotten righteousness and turned against your lord—you will die any day now.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqi cursed him: "You have forgotten righteousness and turned against your lord. You will die any day now.

sentences.zh: 吾教子以順，殺身庸何悔？

translations.literal: I taught my son to follow the righteous path—what regret is there in dying for it?
translations.idiomatic: I taught my son to follow the righteous path. What regret is there in dying for it?

sentences.zh: 鈞死，愈爾遠矣！」

translations.literal: When Jun died, you were far worse than he!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Jun died, you were far worse than he!"

sentences.zh: 悅怒，奮而起。

translations.literal: Yue was enraged and sprang to his feet.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue flew into a rage and sprang to his feet.

sentences.zh: 令奇臨刑，色不變，年七十九，夷其家。

translations.literal: Facing execution, Lingqi's countenance did not change. He was seventy-nine years old; his whole family was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Lingqi's countenance did not change. He was seventy-nine. His whole family was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 燧署璘為軍副，詔拜特進，封義陽郡王。

translations.literal: Sui appointed Lin army deputy; an edict made him Special Grand Master and enfeoffed him as Prince of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui appointed Lin army deputy. An edict made him Special Grand Master and enfeoffed him as Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 既聞父見害，號絕泣血，燧表其冤，加檢校左散騎常侍，賜晉陽第一區、祁田五十頃，贈令奇戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When he learned that his father had been killed, he cried out and wept blood. Sui memorialized on his behalf; he was made Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalier and given the finest residence in Jinyang and fifty qing of fields in Qi. Lingqi was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned his father had been killed, he cried out until he wept blood. Ma Sui memorialized on his behalf. He was made acting Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalier and given the finest residence in Jinyang and fifty qing of fields in Qi. Lingqi was posthumously appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 令奇子 璘璘字元亮。

translations.literal: Lingqi's son Lin—Lin's style was Yuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqi's son Lin, whose style was Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 李懷光反，詔燧討之。

translations.literal: When Li Huaiguang rebelled, an edict ordered Sui to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiguang rebelled, an edict ordered Ma Sui to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 璘介五千兵先濟河，與西師合。

translations.literal: Lin led five thousand troops to cross the river first and joined the western army.
translations.idiomatic: Lin led five thousand troops across the river first and joined the western army.

sentences.zh: 從燧入朝，為輔國大將軍，賜靖恭裏第一區、藍田田四十頃。

translations.literal: He followed Sui to court, was made Grand General Who Assists the State, and was granted the finest residence on Jinggong Lane and forty qing of fields in Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ma Sui to court, was made Grand General Who Assists the State, and was granted the finest residence on Jinggong Lane and forty qing of fields in Lantian.

sentences.zh: 璘之降，母匿里中獨免，及悅死，詔迎於魏，賜宴別殿。

translations.literal: When Lin surrendered, his mother hid in the neighborhood and alone escaped harm. When Yue died, an edict summoned her to Wei and granted her a feast in a separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin surrendered, his mother hid in the neighborhood and alone escaped harm. When Tian Yue died, an edict summoned her to Wei and granted her a feast in a separate hall.

sentences.zh: 璘居環衛十三年，卒，年六十五，贈越州都督。

translations.literal: Lin served in the palace guard for thirteen years, then died at sixty-five; he was posthumously made Regional Commander of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin served in the palace guard for thirteen years, then died at sixty-five. He was posthumously appointed regional commander of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 劉乃劉乃字永夷，河南伊闕人。

translations.literal: Liu Nai—Nai's style was Yongyi; he was a native of Yique in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Nai, whose style was Yongyi, was a native of Yique in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少警穎，警誦《六經》，日數千言。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and quick; he could recite the Six Classics from memory, several thousand words a day.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and could recite the Six Classics from memory, several thousand words a day.

sentences.zh: 善文詞，為時推目。

translations.literal: He excelled at literary composition and was singled out by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at literary composition and was highly regarded in his day.

sentences.zh: 天寶中擢進士第。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 喪父，以孝聞。

translations.literal: When his father died, he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he became known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 服終，中書舍人宋昱知銓事，乃方調，因進書曰：《書》稱：『知人則哲，能官人則惠。』

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Song Yu of the Secretariat was in charge of selection; Nai was about to be assigned a post and therefore submitted a letter, saying: The Documents states: "He who knows men is wise; he who can place men in office is benevolent."
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, Song Yu of the Secretariat was in charge of appointments. Nai was about to receive his first posting and submitted a letter: The Documents says, "He who knows men is wise; he who can place men in office is benevolent."

sentences.zh: 此唐虞以為難。

translations.literal: Even Yao and Shun of Tang and Yu regarded this as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao and Shun regarded this as difficult.

sentences.zh: 今文部始掄材，終授位，是知人、官人，兩任其責。

translations.literal: Now the Ministry of Rites begins by selecting talent and ends by conferring office—thus knowing men and placing men in office, it bears both responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Ministry of Rites selects talent at the start and confers office at the end, bearing both the responsibility to know men and to place them in office.

sentences.zh: 昔禹、稷、臯陶之聖，猶曰載采有九德，考績以九載。

translations.literal: In former times the sages Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao still said one must broadly gather the nine virtues and assess achievement over nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Even the sages Yu, Ji, and Gao Yao said one must broadly gather the nine virtues and assess achievement over nine years.

sentences.zh: 今有司獨委一二小宰，察言於一幅之判，觀行於一揖之內，何其易哉？

translations.literal: Now the authorities entrust this solely to one or two minor officials, judging words from a single sheet of examination composition and observing conduct within one bow—how easy is that?
translations.idiomatic: Today the authorities leave this to one or two minor officials, judging words from a single examination essay and observing conduct within one bow. How easy is that?

sentences.zh: 夫判者，以狹詞短韻為體，是以小冶鼓眾金，雖欲為鼎鏞，不可得已。

translations.literal: Examination compositions take narrow phrasing and short rhymes as their form—like a small smithy beating many metals together: though one wishes to make a great tripod cauldron, it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Examination essays take narrow phrasing and short rhymes as their form, like a small smithy beating many metals together. Though one wishes to forge a great cauldron, it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 故雖有周公、尼父圖書《易象》之訓，以判責之，曾不及徐、庾；

translations.literal: Thus though one has the teachings of the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, the Documents, and the Changes in Images, if judged by examination composition one would not even match Xu Ling and Yu Xin;
translations.idiomatic: Thus though one has the teachings of the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, the Documents, and the Changes, judged by examination essay one would not even match Xu Ling and Yu Xin;

sentences.zh: 雖有至德，以喋喋取之，曾不若嗇夫。

translations.literal: though one has supreme virtue, if selected by glib chatter one would not even match the stingy farmer.
translations.idiomatic: though one has supreme virtue, if selected by glib chatter one would not even match the stingy farmer of the histories.

sentences.zh: 故幹霄蔽日，巨樹也，求尺寸之材，必後於椓杙；

translations.literal: Thus a great tree that reaches the sky and blots out the sun, when inch-sized timber is sought, must come after pounding-stakes and pegs;
translations.idiomatic: Thus a great tree that reaches the sky, when inch-sized timber is sought, must rank below pounding-stakes and pegs;

sentences.zh: 龍吟虎嘯，希聲也，尚頰舌之感，必下於蛙黽。

translations.literal: the dragon's cry and tiger's roar are rare sounds, yet if cheek-and-tongue impressions are still prized, they must rank below frogs and toads.
translations.idiomatic: the dragon's cry and tiger's roar are rare sounds, yet if glib impressions are prized, they must rank below frogs and toads.

sentences.zh: 豈不悲乎！

translations.literal: Is this not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not lamentable!

sentences.zh: 執事誠能先政事，次文學，退觀其治家，進察其臨節，則龐鴻深沈之事，亦可窺其門閾矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Excellency can truly put governance first and literature second, observe how a man manages his household in private and how he meets crisis in public, then even matters as vast and deep as the sky may be glimpsed at the threshold."
translations.idiomatic: If you can truly put governance first and literature second, observe how a man manages his household in private and how he meets crisis in public, then even the deepest matters may be glimpsed at the threshold."

sentences.zh: 昱嘉之，補剡尉。

translations.literal: Yu praised it and appointed him Assistant Magistrate of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yu praised it and appointed him assistant magistrate of Shan.

sentences.zh: 劉晏在江西，奏使巡覆，充留後。

translations.literal: When Liu Yan was in Jiangxi, he memorialized to send Nai on an inspection tour and appointed him acting regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan was in Jiangxi, he memorialized to send Nai on an inspection tour and appointed him acting regional commander.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，召拜司門員外郎。

translations.literal: During the Dali era he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Gate Guards Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign he was summoned and appointed vice director of the Gate Guards Bureau.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，進郭子儀為尚父。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dezong's reign, Guo Ziyi was advanced to the title of Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dezong's reign, Guo Ziyi was advanced to the title of Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 時冊禮廢，視詔文者不適所宜，宰相崔祐甫召乃至閤草之，少選成文，詞義典裁。

translations.literal: At that time enfeoffment rites had fallen into disuse; those who viewed the edict text found it ill-suited. Chief Minister Cui Youfu summoned Nai to the privy chamber to draft it; in a short while the text was complete, its wording and meaning classical and measured.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment rites had fallen into disuse and the draft edict was ill-suited. Chief Minister Cui Youfu summoned Nai to the privy chamber to draft it. In a short while the text was complete, classical and measured in wording and meaning.

sentences.zh: 俄擢給事中，權知兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and given acting charge of the post of Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and given acting charge of the post of Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 楊炎、盧杞當國，五歲不遷。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan and Lu Qi held power, he received no promotion for five years.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan and Lu Qi held power, he received no promotion for five years.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，真拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong he was formally appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jianzhong reign he was formally appointed Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 帝狩奉天，乃臥疾私第，朱泚遣人召之，固稱篤。

translations.literal: When the Emperor hunted at Fengtian, Nai took to his sickbed at his private residence. Zhu Ci sent men to summon him, but he firmly claimed grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor withdrew to Fengtian, Nai took to his sickbed at home. Zhu Ci sent men to summon him, but he firmly claimed grave illness.

sentences.zh: 復遣偽相蔣鎮慰誘，乃佯喑不答，灸無完膚。

translations.literal: Ci again sent the false chancellor Jiang Zhen to console and entice him; Nai feigned muteness and would not answer, and moxibustion left no patch of skin intact.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci again sent the false chancellor Jiang Zhen to console and entice him. Nai feigned muteness and would not answer, and moxibustion left no patch of skin intact.

sentences.zh: 鎮再至，知不可脅，乃太息曰：「我嘗忝曹郎，不能死，寧以自辱亶腥，復欲汙賢哲乎？」

translations.literal: When Zhen came again and saw he could not be coerced, he sighed deeply and said: "I once held the post of Bureau Director and could not die for my principles—would I now disgrace myself further and also defile a man of wisdom?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen came again and saw he could not be coerced, he sighed deeply and said, "I once held a bureau directorship and could not die for my principles. Would I now disgrace myself further and also defile a man of wisdom?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He then stopped.

sentences.zh: 乃聞車駕如梁州，自投於床，搏膺呼天，不食卒，年六十。

translations.literal: When he heard that the imperial carriage was bound for Liangzhou, he threw himself upon his bed, beat his breast, and cried to Heaven; he ate nothing and died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the imperial carriage was bound for Liangzhou, he threw himself upon his bed, beat his breast, and cried to Heaven. He ate nothing and died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其忠，贈禮部尚書，謚曰貞惠。

translations.literal: The Emperor, learning of his loyalty, posthumously made him Minister of Rites and gave the posthumous title Zhenhui (Upright and Kind).
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, learning of his loyalty, posthumously appointed him Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Zhenhui, Upright and Kind.

sentences.zh: 子伯芻，別傳。

translations.literal: His son Bochu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bochu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 孟華孟華，史失其何所人。

translations.literal: Meng Hua—Hua's native place is lost in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hua's native place is not recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 初事李寶臣為府官屬，論議幸幸不回，同舍疾之。

translations.literal: He first served Li Baochen as a staff official; in discussion he was clever and unyielding, and his colleagues in the bureau resented him.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Li Baochen on his staff. In discussion he was clever and unyielding, and his colleagues resented him.

sentences.zh: 王武俊斬李惟嶽，遣華至京師陳事，德宗問河朔利害，華對稱旨，擢檢校兵部郎中兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun killed Li Weiyue and sent Hua to the capital to report affairs. Dezong asked about the advantages and disadvantages of Hebei; Hua's answers pleased him, and he was promoted to Acting Director of the War Bureau and concurrent Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun killed Li Weiyue and sent Hua to the capital to report affairs. Dezong asked about the strategic situation in Hebei. Hua's answers pleased him, and he was promoted to acting director of the War Bureau and concurrent investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 朱滔與武俊謀解田悅之圍，帝詔華還諭，欲亂其謀。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao and Wujun plotted to lift the siege of Tian Yue; the Emperor ordered Hua to return and instruct them, intending to disrupt their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao and Wujun plotted to lift the siege of Tian Yue. The Emperor ordered Hua to return and instruct them, intending to disrupt their plan.

sentences.zh: 華至，讓武俊曰：「安、史未覆滅時，大夫觀其兵，自謂天下可取，今日何汩汩？

translations.literal: When Hua arrived, he reproached Wujun, saying: "Before An and Shi were destroyed, Your Lordship looked on their armies and thought the realm could be taken—why are you so mired today?
translations.idiomatic: When Hua arrived, he reproached Wujun: "Before An and Shi were destroyed, you looked on their armies and thought the realm could be taken. Why are you so mired today?

sentences.zh: 且上於大夫恩甚厚，將還康中丞他州，而歸我深、趙。

translations.literal: Moreover the sovereign's favor toward Your Lordship is very great: he will return Vice Commissioner Kang to another province and restore Shen and Zhao to us.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Emperor's favor toward you is very great. He will return Vice Commissioner Kang to another province and restore Shen and Zhao to us.

sentences.zh: 自古忠臣，未有不先大功而後得高官者。

translations.literal: Since antiquity no loyal minister has failed to win great merit first and only afterward receive high office.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity no loyal minister has won high office before earning great merit.

sentences.zh: 大夫何望於失地邪？

translations.literal: What does Your Lordship hope for in lost territory?
translations.idiomatic: What do you hope for in lost territory?

sentences.zh: 夫藥苦口者利病，大夫後日思愚言，悔無逮！」

translations.literal: Medicine that bitterly stings the mouth benefits the illness—Your Lordship will one day recall my foolish words and regret that it is too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Medicine that bitterly stings the mouth benefits the illness. One day you will recall my words and regret that it is too late!"

sentences.zh: 或曰：「華入朝私奏便宜，欲傾我，故得顯職。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "When Hua went to court he privately memorialized expedient measures to undermine us—that is why he received a prominent post."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "When Hua went to court he privately memorialized measures to undermine us. That is why he received a prominent post."

sentences.zh: 武俊惑之，然以華舊人，未忍奪其職，卒進援悅。

translations.literal: Wujun was swayed, yet because Hua was an old associate he could not bear to strip him of his post and in the end advanced to relieve Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was swayed, yet because Hua was an old associate he could not bear to strip him of his post and in the end advanced to relieve Tian Yue.

sentences.zh: 華從至臨清，稱病還恒州。

translations.literal: Hua followed as far as Linqing, then claimed illness and returned to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hua followed as far as Linqing, then claimed illness and returned to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 武俊令子察所為，乃闔門謝賓客。

translations.literal: Wujun had his son investigate Hua's conduct; Hua thereupon shut his gates and declined visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun had his son investigate Hua's conduct. Hua thereupon shut his gates and declined visitors.

sentences.zh: 武俊知不足忌，無殺華意。

translations.literal: Wujun knew there was nothing to fear and had no intention of killing Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun knew there was nothing to fear and had no intention of killing Hua.

sentences.zh: 既僭稱王，授禮部侍郎，不肯起，嘔血死。

translations.literal: After he had presumptuously declared himself king, [Hua] was appointed Vice Minister of Rites but refused to rise [to accept]; he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Wujun had presumptuously declared himself king, Meng Hua was appointed vice minister of rites but refused to accept the post; he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 張伾張伾者，本為澤潞將，守臨洺，田悅攻之，乘城固守累月，士死，糧且盡，救不至。

translations.literal: Zhang Pi—Pi had originally been a general of Zhe-Lu, defending Linming; Tian Yue attacked him; mounting the walls he held firm for months—soldiers died, provisions were nearly exhausted, and relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pi had originally been a general of Zhe-Lu, defending Linming. When Tian Yue attacked, he mounted the walls and held firm for months. His soldiers died, provisions ran nearly out, and no relief came.

sentences.zh: 伾悉召部將立軍門，命女出遍拜，因曰：「諸君戰良苦，吾無貲為賞，願以是女賣直，為眾士一日費。」

translations.literal: Pi summoned all his subordinate generals to stand at the army gate, had his daughter come out and bow to each in turn, and said: "Gentlemen, you have fought with great hardship; I have no funds for rewards—I wish to sell this daughter for a fair price to cover one day's expenses for all the men."
translations.idiomatic: Pi summoned all his subordinate generals to the army gate, had his daughter come out and bow to each of them, and said, "You have fought with great hardship. I have no money for rewards. I wish to sell this daughter at a fair price to cover one day's expenses for all of you.

sentences.zh: 士皆哭曰：「請死戰！」

translations.literal: The soldiers all wept and said: "We beg to fight to the death!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers all wept and cried, "We beg to fight to the death!"

sentences.zh: 會馬燧自河東將兵擊悅城下，敗之，伾乘勝出戰，無不一當百。

translations.literal: Just then Ma Sui led troops from Hedong and attacked Yue below the city walls, defeating him; Pi seized the victory and sallied forth—each man fought as one against a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ma Sui led troops from Hedong and attacked Tian Yue below the walls, defeating him. Pi seized the victory and sallied forth; each of his men fought as if a hundred.

sentences.zh: 以功遷泗州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was transferred to prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 居州十年，擢右金吾衛大將軍，未拜卒，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: After ten years in the prefecture he was promoted to Great General of the Right Gold Crow Guard; before he could assume the appointment he died, and was posthumously granted Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years in office he was promoted to great general of the Right Gold Crow Guard. Before he could assume the post he died and was posthumously granted right vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 軍中議立其子重政，母徐及兄號訴不肯從，奔告淮南節度使王鍔，乃免。

translations.literal: The army discussed installing his son Chongzheng; his mother Xu and elder brother wailed and pleaded, refusing to comply; they fled to report to Huainan Military Commissioner Wang E, and [Chongzheng] was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The army discussed installing his son Chongzheng as leader. His mother Xu and elder brother wailed in protest and refused to go along; they fled to report to Huainan military commissioner Wang E, and only then were they spared.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其忠，起為金吾衛大將軍，委鍔處以劇職，封徐魯國夫人。

translations.literal: An edict praised their loyalty; [Chongzheng] was raised to Great General of the Gold Crow Guard; Wang E was entrusted to assign him a strenuous post; Xu was enfeoffed as Lady of Lu in Lu State.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised their loyalty. Chongzheng was appointed great general of the Gold Crow Guard, and Wang E was entrusted to assign him a demanding post. Xu was enfeoffed as Lady of Lu.

sentences.zh: 周曾周曾者，本李希烈部將，與王玢、姚詹韋清誌相善，號四公子。

translations.literal: Zhou Ceng—Ceng had originally been a subordinate general of Li Xilie; he was on good terms with Wang Bin, Yao Dan, and Wei Qingzhi, and they were called the Four Young Lords.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ceng had originally been a subordinate general of Li Xilie. He was close to Wang Bin, Yao Dan, and Wei Qingzhi, and they were known as the Four Young Lords.

sentences.zh: 希烈反，曾密得其計，一二以告李勉。

translations.literal: When Xilie rebelled, Ceng secretly learned his plans and reported them one by one to Li Mian.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled, Zhou Ceng secretly learned his plans and reported them one by one to Li Mian.

sentences.zh: 玢為許州鎮遏使。

translations.literal: Bin was Military Stabilization Commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin served as military stabilization commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會哥舒曜拔汝州，希烈遣曾往拒。

translations.literal: When Geshu Yao captured Ruzhou, Xilie dispatched Ceng to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Geshu Yao captured Ruzhou, Li Xilie dispatched Zhou Ceng to resist him.

sentences.zh: 曾欲引軍據蔡，使玢為應，憺、清居中謀取希烈，密求藥毒希烈，不死。

translations.literal: Ceng wished to lead the army to seize Cai and have Bin coordinate from outside; Dan and Qing, stationed centrally, plotted to take Xilie—they secretly sought poison to kill Xilie, but he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ceng planned to lead the army to seize Cai while Wang Bin coordinated from outside. Yao Dan and Wei Qing, stationed at the center, plotted to overthrow Li Xilie; they secretly sought poison to kill him, but he did not die.

sentences.zh: 曾之行，希烈使假子十人從。

translations.literal: When Ceng set out, Xilie had ten adopted sons accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Ceng set out, Li Xilie had ten adopted sons accompany him.

sentences.zh: 次襄城，知其謀，以告。

translations.literal: When they reached Xiangcheng, [the adopted sons] learned of the plot and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Xiangcheng, the adopted sons learned of the plot and reported it.

sentences.zh: 希烈使李克誠率騾軍千人劫曾殺之，而收其兵，並殺玢、憺。

translations.literal: Xilie sent Li Kecheng at the head of a thousand mule-cavalry to intercept and kill Ceng, then took over his troops, and also killed Bin and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie sent Li Kecheng at the head of a thousand mule-cavalry to intercept and kill Zhou Ceng, then took over his troops and also killed Wang Bin and Yao Dan.

sentences.zh: 始，約事覺毋相引。

translations.literal: From the start they had agreed that if the affair were discovered, none would implicate the others.
translations.idiomatic: From the outset they had agreed that if the plot were discovered, none would implicate the others.

sentences.zh: 清懼，陽說希烈曰：「今兵寡，恐不能就事，請乞師朱滔。」

translations.literal: Qing was afraid; he pretended to persuade Xilie, saying: "Our forces are few now—we may not accomplish the affair; I request permission to ask Zhu Tao for reinforcements."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing was afraid. He pretended to persuade Li Xilie, saying, "Our forces are too few now—we may not succeed. I request permission to ask Zhu Tao for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 希烈然之。

translations.literal: Xilie agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie agreed.

sentences.zh: 至襄邑，奪劉洽。

translations.literal: Arriving at Xiangyi, he seized Liu Qia.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xiangyi, he captured the Tang general Liu Qia.

sentences.zh: 德宗贈曾太尉，玢司徒，憺工部尚書，擢清安定郡王，實封戶二百。

translations.literal: Dezong posthumously granted Ceng Grand Preceptor, Bin Minister of Education, and Dan Minister of Works; Qing was elevated to Prince of Anding with two hundred taxable households as fief.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong posthumously granted Zhou Ceng the title of grand preceptor, Wang Bin minister of education, and Yao Dan minister of works. Wei Qing was elevated to Prince of Anding with a fief of two hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 又有呂賁、康秀琳、梁興朝、賈樂卿、侯仙欽皆死希烈之難，贈賁、秀琳尚書左右僕射，興朝等皆秩尚書，遣蕭昕致祭境上。

translations.literal: Also Lü Fen, Kang Xiulin, Liang Xingchao, Jia Leqing, and Hou Xianqin all died in the disaster with Xilie; Fen and Xiulin were posthumously granted Left and Right Vice Ministers of Works; Xingchao and the others were ranked as ministers; Xiao Xin was sent to offer sacrifices at the border.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Fen, Kang Xiulin, Liang Xingchao, Jia Leqing, and Hou Xianqin also died in Li Xilie's rebellion. Fen and Xiulin were posthumously granted left and right vice ministers of works; Xingchao and the others were given ministerial rank; and Xiao Xin was sent to offer sacrifices at the border.

sentences.zh: 命李勉、哥舒曜訪其家子孫，詔雖三世有罪，常降一等。

translations.literal: Li Mian and Geshu Yao were ordered to visit their families' descendants; an edict decreed that though guilt might extend three generations, [their descendants' punishments] would always be reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian and Geshu Yao were ordered to visit the descendants of their families. An edict decreed that even if guilt extended three generations, their descendants' punishments would always be reduced one grade.

sentences.zh: 曾無後，貞元中，女及曾兄子酆爭襲封，有司奏曾首謀歸順，身死賊手，陛下錫真食，不幸絕嗣，宜令酆以五十戶奉祀，女亦封五十戶。

translations.literal: Ceng had no male heir; in the Zhenyuan era, his daughter and his elder brother's son Feng disputed the inherited fief; the authorities memorialized that Ceng was first to plot surrender to the dynasty, died at rebel hands, and Your Majesty granted actual fief—unfortunately the line ended; Feng should receive fifty households for sacrificial maintenance, and the daughter should also be enfeoffed with fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ceng had no male heir. In the Zhenyuan era his daughter and his elder brother's son Feng disputed the inherited fief. The authorities memorialized that Ceng had been first to plot surrender to the dynasty and had died at rebel hands; the Emperor had granted him a fief, but unfortunately the line had ended. Feng should receive fifty households for sacrificial maintenance, and the daughter should also be enfeoffed with fifty households.

sentences.zh: 張名振張名振，李事李懷光為都將。

translations.literal: Zhang Mingzhen—Mingzhen served Li Huaiguang as a chief general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingzhen served Li Huaiguang as a chief general.

sentences.zh: 始，懷光已立功，德宗賜鐵券，奉詔倨甚。

translations.literal: Initially, after Huaiguang had already achieved merit, Dezong bestowed an iron certificate of indemnity; yet in receiving the imperial command he was very arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, after Li Huaiguang had already won great merit, Dezong bestowed an iron certificate of indemnity on him. Yet in receiving the imperial command he was extremely arrogant.

sentences.zh: 名振到軍門大言曰：「太尉見賊不擊，使到不迎，將反邪？

translations.literal: Mingzhen arrived at the army gate and spoke loudly: "Grand Preceptor, you see the rebels but will not attack; when the envoy arrives you do not welcome him—do you intend rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingzhen arrived at the army gate and shouted, "Grand Preceptor, you see the rebels but will not attack them. When the imperial envoy arrives you do not welcome him. Do you intend to rebel?

sentences.zh: 且安、史、仆固等今皆族滅，公欲何為？

translations.literal: Moreover An, Shi, Pugu, and the rest have now all been exterminated to the last clan—what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover An Lushan, Shi Siming, Pugu Huai'en, and the rest have now all been exterminated to the last clan. What do you intend?

sentences.zh: 是資忠義士立功耳。」

translations.literal: This is merely giving loyal and righteous men the chance to achieve merit."
translations.idiomatic: This is merely giving loyal and righteous men the chance to win merit.

sentences.zh: 懷光召見，諭以賊強，須蓄銳俟時，誘為不反。

translations.literal: Huaiguang summoned him for an audience, explaining that the rebels were strong and he must hoard his edge and await the moment, coaxing him into believing he would not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang summoned him and explained that the rebels were strong and he must conserve his strength and await the right moment, coaxing him into believing he would not rebel.

sentences.zh: 及引軍入咸陽，又曰：「公不反，來此何邪？

translations.literal: When he led his army into Xianyang, [Mingzhen] said again: "If you do not rebel, why have you come here?
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiguang led his army into Xianyang, Zhang Mingzhen said again, "If you do not intend to rebel, why have you come here?

sentences.zh: 不急攻泚收京城，欲以賊誰遺？」

translations.literal: You do not urgently attack Zhu Ci and recover the capital—you intend to leave the rebels to whom?"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not urgently attack Zhu Ci and recover the capital, to whom do you intend to leave the rebels?

sentences.zh: 懷光怒曰：「病狂人也。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang raged: "A madman sick with delirium."
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang raged, "A raving madman."

sentences.zh: 使左右拉殺之。

translations.literal: He had his attendants tear him apart and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He had his attendants tear Zhang Mingzhen apart and kill him.

sentences.zh: 石演芬石演芬者，本西域胡人，事懷光至都將，尤親信，畜為假子。

translations.literal: Shi Yanfen—Yanfen was originally a barbarian from the Western Regions; serving Huaiguang he rose to chief general, was especially trusted, and was taken in as an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanfen was originally a man from the Western Regions. Serving Li Huaiguang he rose to chief general, was especially trusted, and was taken in as an adopted son.

sentences.zh: 懷光軍三橋，將與朱泚連和。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's army was at Sanqiao; he was about to ally with Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang's army was at Sanqiao, and he was about to ally with Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 演芬使客郜成義到行在，言懷光無破賊意，請罷其總統。

translations.literal: Yanfen sent a client, Gao Chengyi, to the mobile court to say that Huaiguang had no intent to destroy the rebels and to request that his overall command be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanfen sent a client, Gao Chengyi, to the mobile court to report that Li Huaiguang had no intention of destroying the rebels and to request that his overall command be removed.

sentences.zh: 成義走告懷光子隹，懷光召演芬罵曰：「爾為我子，奈何欲破吾家？

translations.literal: Chengyi fled to tell Huaiguang's son Sui; Huaiguang summoned Yanfen and cursed him: "You are my son—how dare you seek to destroy my house?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chengyi fled to tell Li Huaiguang's son Sui. Huaiguang summoned Shi Yanfen and cursed him, "You are my son—how dare you seek to destroy my house?

sentences.zh: 今日負我，宜即死。」

translations.literal: This day you have wronged me; you ought straightway to die."
translations.idiomatic: Today you betray me—you ought to die at once.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天子以公為股肱，公以我為腹心；

translations.literal: He replied: "The Son of Heaven treats you as arm and thigh; you treat me as heart and belly;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Son of Heaven treats you as his arm and thigh; you treat me as your heart and belly.

sentences.zh: 公乃負天子，我何不負公？

translations.literal: you betray the Son of Heaven—why should I not betray you?
translations.idiomatic: You betray the Son of Heaven—why should I not betray you?

sentences.zh: 且我胡人，無異心，惟知事一人，不呼我為賊，死固吾分。」
