translations.literal: Moreover I am a Hu barbarian, without divided loyalty; I know only to serve one master—if you do not call me a rebel, death is indeed my lot."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as a Hu man I have no divided loyalty—I know only to serve one master. You may not call me a rebel; death is my rightful portion."

sentences.zh: 懷光使士臠食之，皆曰：「烈士也，可令快死。」

translations.literal: Huaiguang had soldiers hack him to pieces; they all said: "A martyr—let him die quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang had his soldiers hack him to pieces. They all said, "A martyr—let him die quickly."

sentences.zh: 以刀斷其頸。

translations.literal: They severed his neck with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: They severed his neck with a blade.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞，贈演芬兵部尚書，賜其家錢三百萬，斬成義於朔方。

translations.literal: When Dezong heard, he posthumously granted Yanfen Minister of War, gave his family three million cash, and executed Chengyi at Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong heard, he posthumously granted Shi Yanfen minister of war, gave his family three million cash, and executed Gao Chengyi at Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 吳漵吳漵者，章敬皇后之弟。

translations.literal: Wu Su—Su was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Su was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，詔贈後祖神泉為司徒，父令珪太尉，擢叔父令瑤太子家令、濮陽郡公，令瑜太子諭德、濟陽郡公，漵太子詹事、濮陽郡公，並開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended, an edict posthumously granted the empress's grandfather Shenquan as Minister of Education and her father Linggui as Grand Preceptor; promoted her uncle Lingyao to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household with the title Duke of Puyang; Lingyu as Preceptor of the Heir with Duke of Jiyang; Su as Grand Mentor of the Heir and Duke of Puyang—all with the honorary rank of Grand General with imperial insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong ascended the throne, an edict posthumously granted the empress's grandfather Shenquan the title of minister of education and her father Linggui grand preceptor. Her uncle Lingyao was promoted to supervisor of the heir apparent's household and enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang; Lingyu became preceptor of the heir and Duke of Jiyang; and Su became grand mentor of the heir and Duke of Puyang—all with the honorary rank of grand general with imperial insignia equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 令瑤兄弟故為縣令、郎將矣，而漵用盛王府參軍進，俄遷鴻臚少卿、金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Lingyao and his brothers had previously been county magistrates and brigade generals, but Su advanced through the position of adjutant on the Prince Sheng's household; soon he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial and General of the Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyao and his brothers had previously served as county magistrates and brigade generals, but Su advanced through the post of adjutant on the Prince of Sheng's household. Soon he was transferred to vice director of the Court of State Ceremonial and general of the Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，遷大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he was transferred to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era he was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 漵循循有禮讓，無倨氣矜色，見重朝廷，時以為材當所位，不自戚屬者。

translations.literal: Su was steadily courteous and yielding, without haughty air or proud mien; the court valued him, and at the time people thought his talent matched his station—not because of imperial kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Su was steadily courteous and yielding, without haughty air or proud bearing. The court valued him, and people at the time thought his talent matched his rank—not because he was an imperial relative.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，盧杞、白誌貞皆謂泚有功，不宜首難，得大臣一人持節尉曉，惡且悛。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen both said Ci had merit and should not be first attacked; if a senior minister were sent with imperial insignia to console and instruct him, his evil might yet be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen both argued that Ci had merit and should not be attacked first. If a senior minister were sent with imperial insignia to console and instruct him, his rebellion might yet be reversed.

sentences.zh: 德宗顧左右，無敢行，漵曰：「陛下不以臣亡能，願至賊中諭天子至意。」

translations.literal: Dezong looked about him—none dared go; Su said: "If Your Majesty does not consider me incapable, I wish to enter the rebels' camp and declare the Son of Heaven's full intent."
translations.idiomatic: Dezong looked about him, but none dared go. Wu Su said, "If Your Majesty does not consider me incapable, I wish to enter the rebel camp and convey the Son of Heaven's full intent.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 漵退謂人曰：「吾知死無益而決見賊者，人臣食祿死其難，所也。

translations.literal: Su withdrew and told others: "I know death will not help, yet I resolved to see the rebels because a minister who eats the state's salary ought to die in its crises—that is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Su withdrew and told others, "I know that death will not help, yet I resolved to face the rebels because a minister who eats the state's salary ought to die in its crises—that is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 方危時，安得自計？

translations.literal: When the realm is in crisis, how can one reckon for one's own sake?
translations.idiomatic: In perilous times, how can one think only of oneself?

sentences.zh: 且不使陛下恨下無犯難者。」

translations.literal: And so that Your Majesty would not regret that below him there was none who dared face difficulty."
translations.idiomatic: And so that Your Majesty would not regret that there was no one below you who dared face danger.

sentences.zh: 即日賫詔見泚，具道帝待以不疑者。

translations.literal: That very day he carried the edict to an audience with Ci and fully relayed how the Emperor treated him without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he carried the edict to an audience with Zhu Ci and fully explained how the Emperor treated him without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 而泚業僭逆，故留漵客省不遣，卒被害。

translations.literal: But Ci was already bent on usurpation, so he detained Su in the Guest Bureau and would not release him; in the end Su was killed.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhu Ci was already bent on usurpation, so he detained Wu Su in the Guest Bureau and would not release him. In the end Su was killed.

sentences.zh: 帝悲梗甚，贈太子太保，謚曰忠，賜其家實戶二百，一子五品正員官。

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved deeply; he posthumously granted Su Grand Guardian of the Heir with the posthumous name Loyal, gave his family two hundred taxable households, and one son a regular fifth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grieved deeply. He posthumously granted Wu Su the title of grand guardian of the heir with the posthumous name Loyal, gave his family two hundred taxable households, and appointed one son to a regular fifth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 京師平，官庀其葬。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, officials arranged his burial.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was pacified, the authorities arranged his funeral.

sentences.zh: 子士矩，別傳。

translations.literal: His son Shiju is treated in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiju has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 高沐高沐者，渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Mu—Mu was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mu was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父馮，事宣武李靈耀，假守曹州。

translations.literal: His father Feng served Xuanwu under Li Lingyao as acting administrator of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng served under Li Lingyao of Xuanwu as acting administrator of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 靈耀反，馮密遣人奏賊纖悉，有詔即拜曹州刺史。

translations.literal: When Lingyao rebelled, Feng secretly sent men to report the rebels' intelligence in full; an edict immediately appointed him Prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Lingyao rebelled, Feng secretly sent men to report detailed intelligence on the rebels to the court. An edict immediately appointed him prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 會李正已盜有曹、濮，馮不能自通朝廷，死官下。

translations.literal: When Li Zhengyi seized Caozhou and Puzhou, Feng could not communicate with the court on his own and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhengyi seized Caozhou and Puzhou, Feng could not get word to the court on his own and died in office.

sentences.zh: 沐，貞元中擢進士第，以家托鄆，故李師古辟署判官。

translations.literal: Mu, in the Zhenyuan era, passed the jinshi examination; because his family relied on Yanzhou, Li Shigu recruited him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era Gao Mu passed the jinshi examination. Because his family relied on Yanzhou, Li Shigu recruited him as an administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 師道叛，沐率其僚郭戶、郭航、李公度引古今成敗，前後鐫說，不能入。

translations.literal: When Shidao rebelled, Mu led his colleagues Guo Hu, Guo Hang, and Li Gongdu to cite successes and failures from antiquity to the present, admonishing repeatedly in speech and writing—they could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao rebelled, Gao Mu led his colleagues Guo Hu, Guo Hang, and Li Gongdu in citing examples of success and failure from antiquity to the present, admonishing him repeatedly in speech and writing—but they could not get through to him.

sentences.zh: 師道所厚吏李文會、林英等乘間訴曰：「比悉心憂公家事，而為沐等所疾，公奈何舉十二州地成沐輩千載名乎？」

translations.literal: Shidao's favored officials Li Wenhu and Lin Ying seized an opening to complain: "We have lately devoted ourselves to worry over Your Lordship's household affairs, yet Mu and his sort hate us—how can Your Lordship raise the twelve prefectures merely to make eternal reputations for Mu and company?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao's favored officials Li Wenhu and Lin Ying seized an opening to complain, "We have lately devoted ourselves to your household affairs, yet Gao Mu and his allies resent us. How can you surrender the twelve prefectures merely to win eternal fame for Mu and his friends?

sentences.zh: 由是疏斥沐，令守濮州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mu was estranged and expelled, and ordered to defend Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gao Mu was estranged and expelled, and ordered to defend Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 沐上書盛誇山東煮海之饒，得其地可以富國。

translations.literal: Mu submitted a memorial lavishly praising the wealth of Shandong's salt-boiling; obtaining those lands could enrich the state.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mu submitted a memorial lavishly praising the wealth of Shandong's salt-boiling industry, arguing that obtaining those lands could enrich the state.

sentences.zh: 師道謀皆露。

translations.literal: Shidao's designs were all exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao's designs were all exposed.

sentences.zh: 後英奏事京師，脅邸史言沐以誠款結天子。

translations.literal: Later Lin Ying went to the capital on business; he coerced a hostel clerk to say Mu was sincerely reaching out to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lin Ying went to the capital on business. He coerced a hostel clerk into saying that Gao Mu was sincerely reaching out to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 師道怒，誅沐，而囚戶濮州，守衛苛嚴，凡十年。

translations.literal: Shidao raged, executed Mu, and imprisoned Hu in Puzhou under harsh guard—for ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao flew into a rage, executed Gao Mu, and imprisoned Guo Hu in Puzhou under harsh guard—for ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟拒命，師道引兵攻彭城，敗蕭、沛數縣而還，以緩王師。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji defied orders, Shidao led troops to attack Pengcheng, ravaged several counties in Xiao and Pei, and returned—to slow the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji defied imperial orders, Li Shidao led troops to attack Pengcheng, ravaged several counties in Xiao and Pei, and returned—to slow the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 戶為繒書藏衣絮間，使郭航間道走武寧軍見李願，請奇兵三千浮海搗萊、淄，賊倚海不為備，且居皆罪人，無與守。

translations.literal: Hu wrote a letter on silk and hid it in padding; he sent Guo Hang by secret route to the Wuning Army to see Li Yuan, requesting three thousand elite troops to cross the sea and strike Lai and Zi—the rebels relied on the sea and were unprepared, and the inhabitants were all convicts with no one to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hu wrote a letter on silk and hid it in clothing padding. He sent Guo Hang by secret route to the Wuning Army to see Li Yuan, requesting three thousand elite troops to cross the sea and strike Lai and Zi. The rebels relied on the sea and were unprepared, and the inhabitants were all convicts with no one to defend the region.

sentences.zh: 始，戶畏事泄，署師道所信吏劉諒名以遣，願白諸朝，議者疑師道使為之，不得報。

translations.literal: At first Hu feared the matter would leak; he signed the trusted official Liu Liang's name to send it; Yuan reported it to the court; deliberators suspected Shidao had orchestrated it and gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guo Hu feared the matter would leak, so he signed the name of Liu Liang, an official Li Shidao trusted, to the letter. Li Yuan reported it to the court, but deliberators suspected Shidao had orchestrated it and gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 航不敢循故道，間關回遠還戶所。

translations.literal: Hang dared not return by the old route; he went by roundabout paths over vast distance back to Hu's place.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hang dared not return by the old route. He took a roundabout path over a vast distance back to Guo Hu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，師道召航，戶疑事露，欲引決，航曰：「事覺，吾獨死，君無患。」

translations.literal: Before long Shidao summoned Hang; Hu suspected the affair was exposed and wished to take his own life; Hang said: "If it is discovered, I alone will die—you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Shidao summoned Guo Hang. Guo Hu suspected the affair was exposed and wished to take his own life. Hang said, "If it is discovered, I alone will die—you need not worry.

sentences.zh: 航卒自殺，遂絕。

translations.literal: Hang in the end killed himself, and [the connection] was severed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hang in the end killed himself, and the connection was severed.

sentences.zh: 及王師討師道，諸節度兵四人，而彭城兵下魚臺金鄉、李聽軍取海州若拾遺，頗用戶策。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shidao with forces from four military commissioners, Pengcheng troops took Yutai and Jinxiang, and Li Ting's army seized Haizhou as easily as picking up lost goods—largely using Hu's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Li Shidao with forces from four military commissioners, Pengcheng troops took Yutai and Jinxiang, and Li Ting's army seized Haizhou as easily as picking up lost goods—largely by using Guo Hu's strategy.

sentences.zh: 初，淮西平，師道勢蹙，內甚懼。

translations.literal: Initially, when Huaixi was pacified, Shidao's position tightened and inwardly he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Huaixi was pacified, Li Shidao's position tightened and inwardly he was greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 李公度與大將李英曇都獻三州。

translations.literal: Li Gongdu together with Grand General Li Yingyan both offered three prefectures in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongdu and the grand general Li Yingyan jointly offered to surrender three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 使長子入侍。

translations.literal: [They proposed] sending the eldest son to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed sending Shidao's eldest son to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 師道然可，俄中悔，欲殺英曇，賈直言諷師道嬖奴曰：「高沐冤氣在天，禍且至。

translations.literal: Shidao agreed at first, but soon repented midway and wished to kill Yingyan; Jia Zhijan hinted to Shidao's favorite slave: "Gao Mu's wronged spirit is in heaven—disaster is near.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao agreed at first, but soon repented and wished to kill Li Yingyan. Jia Zhijan hinted to Shidao's favorite slave, "Gao Mu's wronged spirit is in heaven—disaster is near.

sentences.zh: 英曇復死，是益其崇也。」

translations.literal: If Yingyan dies as well, that will only increase his haunting."
translations.idiomatic: If Li Yingyan dies as well, that will only increase his haunting.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: [Shidao] then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao then stopped.

sentences.zh: 逐於萊州，俄殺之。

translations.literal: [Yingyan] was banished to Laizhou and soon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yingyan was banished to Laizhou and soon killed.

sentences.zh: 又有崔承寵、楊偕、陳佑、崔清皆抗節忤賊，李文會指為沐黨，沐之死，皆被囚。

translations.literal: Also Cui Chengbao, Yang Xie, Chen You, and Cui Qing all upheld integrity and defied the rebels; Li Wenhu denounced them as Mu's faction; at Mu's death they were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chengbao, Yang Xie, Chen You, and Cui Qing also upheld their integrity and defied the rebels. Li Wenhu denounced them as Gao Mu's faction, and after Mu's death they were all imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 劉悟既平師道，捉戶臂歔欷流涕，辟置義成節度府，亦請公度為僚屬。

translations.literal: After Liu Wu had pacified Shidao, he took Hu by the arm, weeping and sighing, and recruited him to the Yicheng military commissioner's staff; he also invited Gongdu as aide.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Wu had pacified Li Shidao, he took Guo Hu by the arm, weeping and sighing, and recruited him to the Yicheng military commissioner's staff. He also invited Li Gongdu as an aide.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年，贈沐吏部尚書，委馬揔備禮收葬，恤其家。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, Mu was posthumously granted Minister of Personnel; Ma Cong was entrusted to prepare rites for reburial and comfort his family.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, Gao Mu was posthumously granted minister of personnel. Ma Cong was entrusted to prepare rites for his reburial and provide relief to his family.

sentences.zh: 航，萊州人，以氣聞，師道署右職，與戶世居齊。

translations.literal: Hang was a man of Laizhou, famed for valor; Shidao appointed him to a high post; he and Hu had lived in Qi for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hang was a native of Laizhou, famed for his valor. Li Shidao appointed him to a high post. He and Guo Hu had lived in Qi for generations.

sentences.zh: 初，戶舉進士，權德輿將取之，聞其家賊中，乃罷，遂為賊聘。

translations.literal: Initially Hu passed the jinshi examination; Quan Deyu was about to select him, but when he heard his family was in rebel territory he abandoned the matter; Hu was then recruited by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Guo Hu passed the jinshi examination. Quan Deyu was about to select him, but when he heard that Hu's family was in rebel territory he abandoned the matter, and Hu was then recruited by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 二人率能以忠顯。

translations.literal: Both men were able to display loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were able to display their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 賈直言賈直言，河朔舊族也，史失其地。

translations.literal: Jia Zhijan—Zhijan was of an old Hebei clan; the histories do not record his birthplace.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhijan was of an old Hebei clan; the histories do not record his birthplace.

sentences.zh: 父道沖，以藝待詔。

translations.literal: His father Daochong served as Artisan Awaiting Imperial Command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daochong served as artisan awaiting imperial command.

sentences.zh: 代宗時，坐事賜鴆，將死，直言紿其父曰：「當謝四方神祇。」

translations.literal: In Daizong's time, for an offense he was granted poison to die; as he was about to die, Zhijan deceived his father: "I must thank the spirits of the four directions."
translations.idiomatic: In Daizong's time, for an offense Daochong was granted poison to die. As he was about to die, Jia Zhijan deceived his father, saying, "I must thank the spirits of the four directions.

sentences.zh: 使者少怠，輒取鴆代飲，迷而踣。

translations.literal: When the envoy relaxed his vigilance for a moment, he snatched the poison and drank in his father's stead; he lost consciousness and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy relaxed his vigilance for a moment, Zhijan snatched the poison and drank it in his father's stead. He lost consciousness and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 明日，毒潰足而出，久乃蘇。

translations.literal: The next day the poison ruptured through his foot and drained out; only after long did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the poison ruptured through his foot and drained out. Only after a long time did he revive.

sentences.zh: 帝憐之，減父死，俱流嶺南。

translations.literal: The Emperor took pity; he commuted his father's death sentence, and both were exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took pity on them. He commuted his father's death sentence, and both father and son were exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 直言由是鐍。

translations.literal: Zhijan from this was lamed.
translations.idiomatic: From that ordeal Jia Zhijan was left lame.

sentences.zh: 後署師道府屬。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed a staff member in Shidao's prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed to Li Shidao's staff.

sentences.zh: 及師道不軌，提刀負棺入諫曰：「願前死，不見城之破。」

translations.literal: When Shidao went astray from the right path, he took up a knife and shouldered a coffin, entering to remonstrate, saying, "I wish to die first—I cannot bear to see the city fall.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao rebelled, he entered bearing a knife and a coffin on his back and admonished him: "Let me die first—I refuse to live to see this city taken.

sentences.zh: 又畫縛載檻車狀而妻子系累者以獻，師道怒，囚之。

translations.literal: He also painted a scene of binding and loading into a caged cart, with wife and children tied together, and presented it. Shidao grew angry and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He also painted a picture of himself bound and loaded into a prison cart, with wife and children shackled together, and presented it. Li Shidao flew into a rage and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 劉悟既入，釋其禁，辟署義成府。

translations.literal: After Liu Wu had entered, he released him from confinement and recruited him to the Yicheng prefectural staff.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Wu took control, he freed him and appointed him to the Yicheng military commissioner's staff.

sentences.zh: 後徙潞，亦隨府遷。

translations.literal: Later, when the office moved to Lu, he also followed the staff in its transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters later moved to Lu Prefecture, he moved with them.

sentences.zh: 監軍劉承偕與悟不平，陰與慈州刺史張汶謀縛悟送闕下，以汶代節度。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Liu Chengjie was at odds with Wu; secretly he joined Cizhou prefect Zhang Wen in a plot to bind Wu and send him to the capital, with Wen replacing him as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Liu Chengjie bore a grudge against Liu Wu and secretly plotted with Cizhou Prefect Zhang Wen to seize Liu Wu and send him to the capital, so that Zhang Wen could take his place as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 事泄，悟以兵圍承偕，殺小使，赴言遽入責曰：「司空縱兵脅天子使者，是欲效李司空邪？

translations.literal: The affair leaked out. Wu surrounded Chengjie with troops and killed his attendants. Zhijan hurried in and rebuked him, saying, "Sikong, you have loosed troops to coerce the Son of Heaven's envoy—do you mean to imitate Sikong Li?
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Liu Wu surrounded Liu Chengjie with troops and killed his attendants. Jia Zhijan rushed in and upbraided him: "Commissioner, you have turned soldiers on the emperor's envoy—are you trying to follow in Li Shidao's footsteps?

sentences.zh: 它日復為軍中所指笑。」

translations.literal: Another day you will again be pointed at and laughed at in the army.
translations.idiomatic: One day the whole army will point at you and laugh.

sentences.zh: 悟聞，感悔，匿承偕於第以免。

translations.literal: Wu heard this, was moved to repentance, and hid Chengjie in his residence to keep him from harm.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu was moved to remorse and hid Liu Chengjie in his own mansion to protect him.

sentences.zh: 悟每有過，必爭，故悟能以臣節光明於朝。

translations.literal: Whenever Wu had a fault, Zhijan was sure to dispute it; therefore Wu was able to make his ministerial integrity shine at court.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liu Wu erred, Jia Zhijan challenged him without fail, and so Liu Wu was able to uphold his loyalty before the throne.

sentences.zh: 穆宗召為諫議大夫，群情灑然稱允。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong summoned him as Remonstrance Grand Master; public sentiment was refreshed and all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong summoned him to serve as Remonstrance Grand Master, and the court received the appointment with universal approval.

sentences.zh: 而悟固留，得聽。

translations.literal: But Wu firmly detained him, and the summons was granted a deferral.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu insisted on keeping him, however, and the court allowed the appointment to wait.

sentences.zh: 始，悟子從諫貴甚，見直言輒衣紫擁笏，以兵自衛。

translations.literal: At first Wu's son Congjian was extremely haughty; whenever he saw Zhijan he would wear purple robes and clutch his court tablet, with soldiers guarding him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Wu's son Liu Congjian carried himself with great arrogance; whenever he saw Jia Zhijan he would appear in purple robes with his court tablet in hand, surrounded by armed guards.

sentences.zh: 直言諫悟曰：「郎少年，毋使襲山東熊，朝服可擅著邪？」

translations.literal: Zhijan remonstrated with Wu, saying, "The young master is still a youth—do not let him take after the brutes of Shandong. May court dress be worn at will?
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhijan admonished Liu Wu: "Your son is still young—do not let him imitate the swaggering warlords of the east. Does he think court robes are his to put on whenever he pleases?

sentences.zh: 悟死，從諫不發喪，召大將劉武德等矯悟遺言，與鄰道使共表求襲位，直言入讓曰：「父死不哭，何顏面見山東義士乎？」

translations.literal: When Wu died, Congjian did not announce the mourning. He summoned the great general Liu Wude and others to forge Wu's last words, and together with envoys from neighboring circuits submitted a memorial requesting succession. Zhijan entered and reproached him, saying, "Your father is dead and you do not weep—what face have you to show the righteous men of Shandong?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wu died, Liu Congjian withheld the news of his death. He summoned the senior general Liu Wude and others to forge his father's dying instructions, then joined with envoys from neighboring circuits in a memorial asking to inherit the post. Jia Zhijan came in and rebuked him: "Your father is dead and you will not mourn—how will you ever face the loyal men of the east?"

sentences.zh: 從諫曰：「欲反耳。」

translations.literal: Congjian said, "I mean to rebel, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian replied, "I intend to rebel—that is all."

sentences.zh: 直言仰天哭曰：「爾父提十二州地歸朝廷為功臣。

translations.literal: Zhijan looked up to heaven and wept, saying, "Your father brought twelve prefectures back to the court and became a meritorious minister.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhijan lifted his face to heaven and wailed: "Your father surrendered twelve prefectures to the throne and died a honored servant of the empire.

sentences.zh: 然以張汶故，自謂不潔淋頭，卒羞死。

translations.literal: Yet because of Zhang Wen he considered himself defiled as if urine had been poured on his head, and in the end died of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of Zhang Wen he felt himself disgraced beyond cleansing and died in humiliation.

sentences.zh: 郎今日乃欲反邪？」

translations.literal: And today you, young master, wish to rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: And now you mean to rebel?"

sentences.zh: 從諫起抱直言項哭曰：「計窮而然。」

translations.literal: Congjian rose, embraced Zhijan by the neck, and wept, saying, "Plans exhausted—that is why it has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian rose, threw his arms around Jia Zhijan's neck, and wept: "I am driven to this because I have no other way out."

sentences.zh: 直言曰：「君何憂無土地，今脅朝廷，正速死耳。

translations.literal: Zhijan said, "My lord, why worry that you lack land? Now you coerce the court—you are merely hastening your death.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhijan said, "Why worry about lacking territory? If you threaten the throne now, you will only bring on your own swift ruin.

sentences.zh: 若從武德謀，吾見劉氏為元濟矣。」

translations.literal: If you follow Wude's plot, I see the Liu house becoming Yuanji."
translations.idiomatic: If you follow Liu Wude's counsel, I see the Liu clan ending as Wu Yuanji did."

sentences.zh: 從諫拜曰：「唯大夫救之。」

translations.literal: Congjian bowed and said, "Only the Grand Master can save me."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian bowed low and said, "Only you can save me, sir."

sentences.zh: 直言乃自攝留後，使從諫居喪。

translations.literal: Zhijan thereupon took the acting post of leave-behind commissioner himself and had Congjian observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhijan then assumed the acting post of military commissioner himself and put Liu Congjian into proper mourning.

sentences.zh: 初，從諫惟鄆兵二千同謀。

translations.literal: At first Congjian had only two thousand Yan troops as co-conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: At first only two thousand Yan troops were in on Liu Congjian's plot.

sentences.zh: 直言既折之，軍中遂安。

translations.literal: Once Zhijan had broken their resolve, the army was thereafter settled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jia Zhijan had broken their resolve, the army settled down.

sentences.zh: 大和九年卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dahe he died; he was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 835 and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 辛讜辛讜者，太原尹雲京孫也。

translations.literal: Xin Zan—Zan was grandson of Taiyuan governor Yin Yunjing.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan was the grandson of the Taiyuan governor Yin Yunjing.

sentences.zh: 學《詩》、《書》，能擊劍，重然諾，走人所急。

translations.literal: He studied the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents, could wield the sword, valued sworn promises, and hastened wherever people were in urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics, was skilled with the sword, held his word sacred, and always rushed to help those in distress.

sentences.zh: 初事李嶧，主錢穀。

translations.literal: At first he served Li Bi, overseeing funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Li Bi, managing finances and supplies.

sentences.zh: 性廉勁，遇事不處文法，皆與之合。

translations.literal: By nature upright and forceful, in handling affairs he did not bind himself to written law, yet all accorded with him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and resolute by nature, he handled matters without fussing over formal procedure, and Li Bi always found himself in agreement with him.

sentences.zh: 罷居揚州，年五十，不肯仕，而慨然常有濟時意。

translations.literal: Dismissed from office, he lived in Yangzhou. At fifty he would not take office, yet he sighed often and always harbored the will to aid the age.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he settled in Yangzhou. At fifty he refused further appointment, yet he burned with the desire to serve the times.

sentences.zh: 龐勛反，攻杜慆於泗州。

translations.literal: Pang Xun rebelled and attacked Du Tao at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun rebelled, he besieged Du Tao at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 讜聞之，挐舟趨泗口，貫賊柵以入。

translations.literal: Zan heard of it, rowed a boat toward the Si River mouth, and pierced through the rebel palisade to enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Zan heard the news, he took a boat to the mouth of the Si River and broke through the rebel barricades to enter the city.

sentences.zh: 慆素聞其名，握手曰：「吾僚李延樞嘗為吾道夫子為人，何意臨教？

translations.literal: Tao had long heard his name and clasped his hand, saying, "My colleague Li Yanshu once described for me the Master's character—what intent brings you here to instruct us?
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao had long known his reputation. He grasped his hand and said, "My colleague Li Yanshu once told me what kind of man you are—what brings you here to guide us?

sentences.zh: 吾無憂矣！」

translations.literal: I have no worries now!
translations.idiomatic: I have nothing left to fear!

sentences.zh: 讜亦謂慆可共事，乃請還與妻子決，同慆生死。

translations.literal: Zan also considered Tao a man with whom one could share the work, and requested to return and bid farewell to wife and children, sharing life and death with Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan also judged Du Tao a man worth standing with. He asked leave to return home and say farewell to his wife and children, pledging to live or die with Du Tao.

sentences.zh: 時賊張甚，眾皆南走，獨讜北行。

translations.literal: At the time the rebels were very strong; the multitude all fled south, while Zan alone went north.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were at the height of their power and everyone was fleeing south—Xin Zan alone headed north toward the siege.

sentences.zh: 讜未至，慆憂之，延樞知必來，曰：「讜至，可表為判官。」

translations.literal: Before Zan arrived, Tao worried about him. Yanshu knew he would surely come and said, "When Zan arrives, he may be memorialized as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xin Zan arrived, Du Tao worried for him. Li Yanshu, certain he would come, said, "When Xin Zan arrives, recommend him as military aide.

sentences.zh: 慆許諾。

translations.literal: Tao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄而至，慆喜曰：「圍急，飛鳥不敢過，君乃冒白刃入危城，古人所不能。」

translations.literal: Soon he arrived. Tao rejoiced and said, "The siege is desperate—even birds dare not pass. Yet you braved naked blades to enter a perilous city—what the ancients could not do.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xin Zan arrived. Du Tao exulted: "The siege is desperate—even birds will not fly over the walls, yet you risked the enemy's blades to enter this doomed city. Not even the heroes of old did such a thing.

sentences.zh: 乃勸解白衣被甲。

translations.literal: He thereupon urged him to remove his white robes and don armor.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged Xin Zan to put off his plain clothes and take up armor.

sentences.zh: 賊將李圓焚淮口，讜曰：「事棘矣，獨出可以求援。」

translations.literal: The rebel general Li Yuan burned the Huai River crossing. Zan said, "Matters are critical—only by going out can we seek relief.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Li Yuan set fire to the Huai River crossing. Xin Zan said, "The situation is desperate—the only hope is to break out and seek reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 乃與楊文播、李行實戊夜逾淮，坎岸登，馳三十里至洪澤，見戍將郭厚本告急。

translations.literal: He then, with Yang Wenbo and Li Xingshi, at the fifth watch of the night crossed the Huai, climbed the bank, and galloped thirty li to Hongze, where he saw the garrison commander Guo Houben and reported the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: He set out with Yang Wenbo and Li Xingshi, crossed the Huai by night, scaled the far bank, and rode thirty li to Hongze to plead for help from the garrison commander Guo Houben.

sentences.zh: 厚本許出兵，大將袁公異等曰：「賊眾我寡，不可往。」

translations.literal: Houben promised to send troops, but the great generals Yuan Gongyi and others said, "The rebels are many and we are few—we cannot go.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Houben agreed to send troops, but his senior officers Yuan Gongyi and others objected: "The enemy outnumber us—we cannot march.

sentences.zh: 讜拔劍瞋目呼曰：「泗州陷在旦夕，公等被詔來，乃逗留不進，欲何為？

translations.literal: Zan drew his sword, glared, and shouted, "Sizhou will fall within the day! You were summoned by imperial decree—yet you linger and do not advance. What do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan drew his sword, glared, and roared: "Sizhou will fall at any moment! The throne sent you here—will you sit idle? What do you mean by this?

sentences.zh: 大丈夫孤國恩，雖生可羞。

translations.literal: A great man who betrays the state's grace—though he lives, it is shameful.
translations.idiomatic: A true man who abandons his sovereign's trust has no honor left in living.

sentences.zh: 且失泗，則淮南為寇場，君尚能獨存？

translations.literal: Moreover, if Si is lost, then Huainan becomes the rebels' hunting ground—can you alone survive?
translations.idiomatic: If Sizhou falls, all Huainan becomes rebel territory—do you think you will survive alone?

sentences.zh: 吾今斷左臂殺君去。」

translations.literal: I will now sever my left arm and kill you before I go."
translations.idiomatic: I will cut off my own left arm and kill you before I leave."

sentences.zh: 推劍直前，厚本持之，公異等僅免。

translations.literal: He thrust his sword and pressed forward. Houben seized him, and Gongyi and the others barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He lunged forward with his sword. Guo Houben held him back, and Yuan Gongyi and the others barely escaped with their lives.

sentences.zh: 讜望泗慟哭，帳下皆流涕。

translations.literal: Zan looked toward Si and wailed; all beneath the tent wept.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan turned toward Sizhou and wept in anguish, and every man in the camp wept with him.

sentences.zh: 厚本決許付兵五百，讜曰：「足矣！」

translations.literal: Houben at last firmly promised five hundred troops. Zan said, "That is enough!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Houben finally committed five hundred men. Xin Zan said, "That is enough!

sentences.zh: 遍問士曰：「能行乎？」

translations.literal: He asked every soldier in turn, "Can you march?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked each soldier in turn, "Will you come with me?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: All said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "We will."

sentences.zh: 讜仆面於地，泣以謝。

translations.literal: Zan prostrated his face to the ground and wept in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan prostrated himself and wept his gratitude.

sentences.zh: 眾既叩淮，有人語曰：「賊破城矣！」

translations.literal: When the force had already struck the Huai, someone called out, "The rebels have taken the city!
translations.idiomatic: As they were crossing the Huai, someone shouted, "The rebels have broken the city!

sentences.zh: 讜將斬之，眾為請。

translations.literal: Zan was about to behead him; the troops pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan was about to cut him down, but the men begged for his life.

sentences.zh: 讜曰：「公等登舟，吾赦其死。」

translations.literal: Zan said, "You gentlemen board the boats—I spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan said, "Board the boats, all of you, and I will spare him.

sentences.zh: 士遽登。

translations.literal: The soldiers hurried aboard.
translations.idiomatic: The men scrambled aboard at once.

sentences.zh: 已濟，慆亦出兵，表裏擊，賊大敗。

translations.literal: Once they had crossed, Tao also sent troops out; attacking from within and without, they routed the rebels completely.
translations.idiomatic: After they crossed the river, Du Tao sallied forth as well. Caught between the two forces, the rebels suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 讜入，人心遂固。

translations.literal: When Zan entered, the people's hearts were thereafter firm.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Zan returned to the city, the defenders' morale was restored.

sentences.zh: 浙西杜審權遣將翟行約赴援，壁蓮塘，慆欲遣人廷勞，諸吏憚不敢出，讜獨往犒而還。

translations.literal: Zhexi's Du Shenquan sent the general Zhai Xingyue to bring relief; he encamped at Liantang. Tao wished to send someone to the camp to pay respects, but the officials all feared and dared not go out—Zan alone went to reward the troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenquan of Zhexi sent the general Zhai Xingyue with reinforcements, and he encamped at Liantang. Du Tao wanted to send an envoy to welcome him, but every official was too afraid to go—only Xin Zan went out alone to bring supplies to the relief force and returned safely.

sentences.zh: 圍三月，救兵外敗，城益危。

translations.literal: The siege lasted three months; relief troops were defeated outside, and the city grew ever more perilous.
translations.idiomatic: After three months under siege, the relief army was beaten outside the walls and the city grew more desperate by the day.

sentences.zh: 讜復請乞兵淮南，與壯士徐珍十人持斧夜斬賊柵出，見節度使令狐，復詣浙西見審權。

translations.literal: Zan again requested to beg troops from Huainan. With ten stalwarts led by Xu Zhen, axes in hand, he by night cut through the rebel palisade and went out, saw Military Commissioner Linghu, then went again to Zhexi to see Shenquan.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan volunteered to seek troops from Huainan. With ten stalwarts including Xu Zhen, axes in hand, he cut through the rebel barricades by night, reached Military Commissioner Linghu Tao, and then traveled on to Zhexi to see Du Shenquan.

sentences.zh: 時皆傳泗州已陷，疑讜為賊計，囚之。

translations.literal: At the time all reported that Sizhou had already fallen; they suspected Zan was acting for the rebels and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors were everywhere that Sizhou had already fallen, and Du Shenquan suspected Xin Zan of working for the rebels and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 讜引李嶧自明。

translations.literal: Zan cited Li Bi to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan invoked Li Bi's testimony to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 嶧時為大同防禦使，稱其忠可信。

translations.literal: Bi was then Defender of Datong and declared his loyalty trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, then Defender of Datong, vouched for his loyalty and trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 審權乃許救，合淮南兵五千，鹽粟具。

translations.literal: Shenquan thereupon agreed to rescue; together with five thousand Huainan troops, salt and grain were fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenquan then agreed to send aid: five thousand Huainan troops with full supplies of salt and grain.

sentences.zh: 方淮路梗，不得進。

translations.literal: Just then the Huai routes were blocked, and they could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: But the Huai River routes were blocked and the relief force could not get through.

sentences.zh: 讜引兵決戰，斬賊六百級，乃克入，城上歡叫，慆與下迎泣，表其功於朝，授監察御史。

translations.literal: Zan led troops in decisive battle, beheaded six hundred rebels, and only then was able to enter. On the walls they shouted for joy; Tao came down to meet him weeping. His merit was memorialized to the court, and he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zan led the relief force in a pitched battle, killed six hundred rebels, and fought his way into the city. The walls erupted in cheers; Du Tao came down to meet him in tears. His exploits were reported to the throne and he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 圍凡十月乃解，卒完一州。

translations.literal: The siege in all lasted ten months before it was lifted; in the end one prefecture was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted ten months in all before it was lifted, and the entire prefecture was saved.

sentences.zh: 初，讜求救也，過家十餘，未嘗見妻子，得糧累二十萬。

translations.literal: At first, when Zan went to seek relief, he passed his home more than ten times yet never once saw wife or children, and obtained grain amounting to two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Zan first set out to seek reinforcements, he passed his own home more than ten times without once stopping to see his wife and children, and raised two hundred thousand units of grain.

sentences.zh: 讜子及兄子客廣陵，托慆曰：「使先人不乏祀，公之惠也。」

translations.literal: Zan's son and his elder brother's son lodged in Guangling and entrusted Tao, saying, "If our forebears lack no sacrifices, it will be your grace.
translations.idiomatic: His son and his brother's son stayed in Guangling, and he entrusted them to Du Tao with the words: "If my ancestors' rites are kept, it will be through your kindness.

sentences.zh: 後以功第一，拜亳州刺史，徙曹、泗二州。

translations.literal: Later, for merit ranked first, he was appointed prefect of Bozhou and transferred among Cao and Si prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Later, ranked first in merit, he was appointed prefect of Bozhou and then transferred to govern Cao and Si prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，終嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu he died as military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qianfu era he died while serving as military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 方讜之少，耕於野，有牛斗，眾畏奔踐，讜直前，兩持其角，牛不能動，久而引觸，竟折其角。

translations.literal: When Zan was young, plowing in the fields, two oxen fought. The crowd feared being trampled and fled; Zan went straight forward, seized both by the horns with both hands, and the oxen could not move. After long he pulled and butted, and at last broke off a horn.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, while plowing in the fields, Xin Zan once saw two oxen fighting. Everyone else fled in fear of being trampled, but he walked straight up, seized both animals by the horns, and held them fast. After a long struggle he wrenched one ox's head aside and snapped off its horn.

sentences.zh: 里人駭異，屠牛以飯讜。

translations.literal: The villagers were astonished and slaughtered an ox to feed Zan.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers were awestruck and slaughtered an ox to feast him.

sentences.zh: 然讜臒短，才及中人。

translations.literal: Yet Zan was thin and short, reaching only to an average man's height.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xin Zan was slight and short—barely of average height.

sentences.zh: 後貴，力亦少衰云。

translations.literal: Later, when he had risen to honor, his strength also somewhat declined, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to high rank, it is said, his strength waned somewhat as well.

sentences.zh: 黃碣黃碣，閩人也。

translations.literal: Huang Jie—Jie was a man of Min.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jie was a native of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 初為閩小將，喜學問，軒然有志向。

translations.literal: At first he was a minor general of Min, fond of learning, with lofty bearing and aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a junior officer in Fujian, loved learning, and carried himself with evident ambition.

sentences.zh: 同列有假其筆者，碣怒曰：「是筆它日斷大事，不可假。」

translations.literal: A comrade asked to borrow his brush. Jie angrily said, "This brush will one day decide great affairs—it cannot be lent.
translations.idiomatic: When a comrade asked to borrow his writing brush, Huang Jie snapped: "This brush will one day decide weighty matters—it is not to be lent.

sentences.zh: 後戰安南有功，高駢表其能，為漳州刺史，徙婺州，治有績。

translations.literal: Later, for merit fighting in Annam, Gao Pian memorialized his ability; he became prefect of Zhangzhou, was transferred to Wuzhou, and his governance had achievement.
translations.idiomatic: After distinguishing himself in campaigns in Annam, Gao Pian recommended his abilities. He was appointed prefect of Zhangzhou, later transferred to Wuzhou, and governed with distinction.

sentences.zh: 劉漢宏遣兵攻之，兵寡不可守，棄州去，客蘇州。

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong sent troops to attack him; his forces were few and the prefecture could not be held. He abandoned the prefecture and went, lodging in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hanhong sent troops against him, his forces were too few to hold the city. He abandoned his post and took refuge in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 董昌為威勝軍節度使，表碣自副，久乃應。

translations.literal: Dong Chang, as military commissioner of the Weisheng Army, memorialized Jie as his deputy; only after long did he respond.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang, military commissioner of the Weisheng Army, invited Huang Jie to serve as his deputy, and only after much urging did he accept.

sentences.zh: 及昌反，碣諫曰：「大王拔田畝，席貢輸之勤，位將相，非有勛業可紀。

translations.literal: When Chang rebelled, Jie remonstrated, saying, "Great King, you rose from the furrowed fields through diligence in paying tribute and now stand as minister and general, yet there is no meritorious achievement to record.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Chang rebelled, Huang Jie admonished him: "Your Majesty rose from the fields through years of paying tribute to the throne and now hold rank as minister and general, yet you have no great deeds to your name.

sentences.zh: 今不能盡忠王朝，乃自尊大，一日誅滅無種矣。

translations.literal: Now you cannot exhaust loyalty to the imperial house, yet instead aggrandize yourself—in a single day extermination will leave no seed.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot serve the dynasty with full loyalty and instead set yourself above it, one day you and your whole line will be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 桓、文不侮周室，曹操弗敢危漢。

translations.literal: Huan and Wen did not insult the house of Zhou; Cao Cao did not dare endanger Han.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi did not humiliate the Zhou royal house, and Cao Cao did not dare threaten the Han dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今王僻嬰一城，乃為大逆，何邪？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, holding only one remote city, yet commit great treason—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you hold one remote city and call yourself emperor—what madness is this?

sentences.zh: 碣請舉族先死，不能見王之滅。」

translations.literal: Jie requested that his whole clan die first—he could not bear to see the King's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jie asked that his entire clan be executed first, saying he could not bear to live to see the king's ruin.

sentences.zh: 昌怒曰：「碣不順我邪？」

translations.literal: Chang angrily said, "Jie, you do not obey me?"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang raged: "Huang Jie, you defy me?"

sentences.zh: 斥出之。

translations.literal: He drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: He had him thrown out.

sentences.zh: 碣移書幕府李滔曰：「『順天』建元，以愚策之，針可為槊邪？」

translations.literal: Jie sent a letter to the staff officer Li Tao, saying, "Establishing the era title 'Obedient to Heaven'—by my dull reckoning, can a needle serve as a spear?
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jie wrote to the staff officer Li Tao: "You have proclaimed the era name 'Obedient to Heaven'—tell me, can a needle pass for a spear?

sentences.zh: 或竊其書示昌，昌令使者斬之。

translations.literal: Someone stole the letter and showed it to Chang; Chang ordered an envoy to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone stole the letter and showed it to Dong Chang, who sent an agent to execute him.

sentences.zh: 使以首至，昌詬曰：「賊負我，三公不肯為，而求死邪？」

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived with the head, Chang cursed, saying, "The traitor failed me—he would not take the rank of the Three Excellencies, yet sought death?
translations.idiomatic: When the agent returned with Huang Jie's head, Dong Chang snarled: "The fool betrayed me—he refused the Three Excellencies and chose death instead?

sentences.zh: 抵混中，夷其家百口，坎鏡湖之南同瘞焉。

translations.literal: He threw it into the muck, exterminated his household of a hundred mouths, and buried them together in a pit south of Mirror Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He tossed the head into the filth, executed his entire household of a hundred souls, and buried them together in a common pit south of Mirror Lake.

sentences.zh: 昌敗，有詔贈司徒，求其後不能得。

translations.literal: When Chang was defeated, an edict posthumously awarded Jie as Grand Preceptor, but his descendants could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Chang's defeat, an edict posthumously made Huang Jie Grand Preceptor, but no descendants could be found.

sentences.zh: 昌已殺碣，滔亦遇害，乃召會稽令吳鐐問策，鐐曰：「王為真諸侯，遺榮子孫而不為，乃作偽天子，自取滅亡。」

translations.literal: Chang had already killed Jie, and Tao also met with harm. He then summoned the Kuaiji magistrate Wu Liao to ask counsel. Liao said, "Your Majesty could have been a true feudal lord, leaving glory to posterity, yet did not—instead playing the false Son of Heaven and bringing destruction on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Chang had killed Huang Jie and Li Tao had also been murdered, he summoned the Kuaiji magistrate Wu Liao for counsel. Wu Liao said, "You could have remained a legitimate feudal lord and passed honor to your descendants—but instead you played at being emperor and have chosen your own ruin.

sentences.zh: 昌叱斬之，族其家。

translations.literal: Chang shouted and had him beheaded, exterminating his household.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang ordered him executed on the spot and wiped out his entire family.

sentences.zh: 又召山陰令張遜知御史臺，固辭曰：「王自棄，為天下笑。

translations.literal: He again summoned the Shanyin magistrate Zhang Xun to take charge of the Censorate. Xun firmly declined, saying: "Your Majesty has cast yourself away and become the laughingstock of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He next summoned the Shanyin magistrate Zhang Xun to head the Censorate. Xun firmly declined: "You have cast yourself away and become the laughingstock of the realm.

sentences.zh: 且六州勢不助逆，王據孤州以速死，謂何？

translations.literal: Moreover the six prefectures will not aid rebellion; Your Majesty holds a lone prefecture only to hasten death—what do you say to that?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the six prefectures will not aid rebellion. You hold a lone prefecture only to hasten your death—what do you say to that?

sentences.zh: 遜不敢以身許王也。」

translations.literal: Xun dares not pledge his person to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not pledge my life to you."

sentences.zh: 昌惡之，曰：「遜不知天意，議邪說拒我。」

translations.literal: Chang hated him and said: "Xun does not know Heaven's will and spreads perverse doctrines to reject me."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang hated him and said, "Xun does not know Heaven's will and spreads perverse doctrines to reject me."

sentences.zh: 囚之。

translations.literal: He imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 他日謂人曰：「我無碣、鐐、遜，何乏事？」

translations.literal: Another day he said to others: "Without Jie, Liao, and Xun, what would I lack in affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day he said to others, "Without Huang Jie, Wu Liao, and Zhang Xun, what would I lack in affairs?"

sentences.zh: 即害之。

translations.literal: He then had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him killed.

sentences.zh: 碣孫 揆孫揆，字聖圭，刑部侍郎逖五世從孫也。

translations.literal: Jie's grandson Kui—Sun Kui, style Shenggui, was a fifth-generation collateral descendant of the Vice Minister of Justice Sun Di.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jie's grandson Sun Kui, whose style was Shenggui, was a fifth-generation collateral descendant of Vice Minister of Justice Sun Di.

sentences.zh: 第進士，辟戶部巡官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was recruited as an itinerant officer of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was recruited as an itinerant officer of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 歷中書舍人、刑部侍郎、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He served successively as Secretariat Drafter, Vice Minister of Justice, and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Secretariat drafter, Vice Minister of Justice, and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 昭宗討李克用，以揆為兵馬招討制置宣慰副使，既而更授昭義軍節度使，以本道兵會戰。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong campaigned against Li Keyong, Kui was made Deputy Commissioner for Pacification, Organization, and Comfort of the Army; shortly afterward he was further appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army and led his command's troops into battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong campaigned against Li Keyong, Kui was made deputy commissioner for army pacification and comfort. Shortly afterward he was appointed military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army and led his command's troops into battle.

sentences.zh: 克用伏兵刀黃嶺，執揆，厚禮而將用之，曰：「公輩當從容廟堂，何為自履行陣也？」

translations.literal: Keyong ambushed him at Daohuang Ridge, seized Kui, treated him with great courtesy and was about to employ him, saying: "Gentlemen like you ought to move at ease in the court halls—why do you walk the ranks yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong ambushed him at Daohuang Ridge and seized him. He treated Kui with great courtesy and was about to employ him, saying, "Men like you ought to move at ease in the court halls. Why do you walk the ranks yourself?"

sentences.zh: 揆大罵不詘，克用怒，使以鋸解之，鋸齒不行，揆謂曰：「死狗奴，解人當束之以板，汝輩安知？」

translations.literal: Kui cursed him loudly and would not yield. Keyong was enraged and had him sawn apart; the saw teeth would not bite. Kui said: "Dead dog-slaves! When dismembering a man one ought to bind him with boards—what do you lot know?"
translations.idiomatic: Kui cursed him loudly and would not yield. Li Keyong was enraged and had him sawn apart, but the saw teeth would not bite. Kui said, "Dead dog-slaves! When dismembering a man you ought to bind him with boards. What do you lot know?"

sentences.zh: 行刑者如其所言，詈聲不輟至死。

translations.literal: The executioners did as he said; his curses did not cease until death.
translations.idiomatic: The executioners did as he said. His curses did not cease until he died.

sentences.zh: 昭宗憐之，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: Zhaozong pitied him and posthumously made him Left Vice President of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong pitied him and posthumously appointed him Left Vice President of the Secretariat.
